```ts
  report.expiredUploads = uploads.length;
  report.timedOutScans = scans.length;
  report.expiredPreviews = previews.length;
  report.stoppedLate = late.length;
  for (const id of [...uploads, ...scans, ...previews, ...late]) await endFiles(deps, id);
  if (uploads.length + scans.length + previews.length + late.length > 0) {
    deps.log.info({ expiredUploads: uploads.length, timedOutScans: scans.length, expiredPreviews: previews.length, stoppedLate: late.length }, "import-drive: time limits");
  }
}

/**
 * Step 8: what a crash between a commit and a file operation left behind, once older than an hour. An archive folder or
 * a queue marker goes unless its import is still uploading or scanning; a work folder is asked for unless its import
 * still needs it; a deletion request is withdrawn once the importer has carried it out and an hour has passed, so a scan
 * that was aborted has long seen it.
 */
async function orphans(deps: ImportDeps, now: Date, report: DriveReport): Promise<void> {
  const at = now.getTime();
  const old = (entries: { id: string; ageMs: number }[]) => entries.filter((entry) => entry.ageMs > IMPORT_RULES.orphanAgeMs);
  const folders = old(await deps.files.archiveFolders(at));
  const markers = old(await deps.files.queueMarkers(at));
  const work = old(await deps.files.workFolders(at));
  const requests = await deps.files.deletionRequests(at);
  const statuses = await deps.repo.statuses([...new Set([...folders, ...markers, ...work].map((entry) => entry.id))]);
  for (const id of new Set([...folders, ...markers].map((entry) => entry.id))) {
    const status = statuses.get(id);
    if (status !== undefined && NEEDS_ARCHIVE.has(status)) continue;
    await deps.files.removeArchive(id);
    report.orphanArchives++;
  }
  const requested = new Set(requests.map((entry) => entry.id));
  for (const { id } of work) {
    const status = statuses.get(id);
    if ((status !== undefined && NEEDS_WORK.has(status)) || requested.has(id)) continue;
    await deps.files.requestWorkDeletion(id);
    report.orphanWork++;
  }
  for (const { id, ageMs } of requests) {
    if (ageMs <= IMPORT_RULES.orphanAgeMs || (await deps.files.workFolderPresent(id))) continue;
    await deps.files.withdrawWorkDeletion(id);
    report.withdrawn++;
  }
  if (report.orphanArchives + report.orphanWork + report.withdrawn > 0) {
    deps.log.warn({ archives: report.orphanArchives, work: report.orphanWork, withdrawn: report.withdrawn }, "import-drive: orphans");
  }
}

/** One round at `now`. */
export async function driveRound(deps: ImportDeps, now: Date, options: DriveOptions): Promise<DriveReport> {
  const report: DriveReport = { ready: 0, failed: 0, expiredUploads: 0, timedOutScans: 0, expiredPreviews: 0, stoppedLate: 0, picksDeleted: 0, rowsDeleted: 0, orphanArchives: 0, orphanWork: 0, withdrawn: 0 };
  await scansDone(deps, now, report, options.caps);
  await timeLimits(deps, now, report);
  const kept = await deps.repo.retention(now);
  report.picksDeleted = kept.picks;
  report.rowsDeleted = kept.rows;
  if (options.orphans) await orphans(deps, now, report);
  return report;
}

/** import-drive as a job: rounds every driveIntervalMs, the lock held for at most driveLockMs past a crash, orphans every tenth round. */
export function createDriveJob(deps: ImportDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  let rounds = 0;
  const job = createJob({
    name: "import-drive",
    intervalMs: IMPORT_RULES.driveIntervalMs,
    lockTtlMs: IMPORT_RULES.driveLockMs,
    lock,
    log: deps.log,
    run: async () => {
      rounds++;
      await driveRound(deps, deps.now(), { orphans: rounds % IMPORT_RULES.orphanEveryRounds === 1 });
    },
  });
  return { round: job.round, start: job.start };
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/imports/files.ts`

```ts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { constants } from "node:fs";
import { lstat, mkdir, open, readdir, rename, rm, statfs, type FileHandle } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import {
  archivesLayout,
  isImportId,
  openWorkFile,
  readHeartbeat,
  readSummary,
  workLayout,
  type JobFile,
  type ReadResult,
  type WorkFileResult,
} from "@korbat/import-protocol";
import type { ImportSummary } from "@korbat/contracts";

/**
 * The API's side of the import's file protocol (3b design, section 7.1), through packages/import-protocol's layouts. The
 * API writes import-archives (the archives as they arrive, each job's job.json, the queue markers and the deletion
 * requests) and only reads import-work, which the importer writes after parsing hostile input: every file of import-work
 * is read through openWorkFile, which trusts no path, link or size the importer left there.
 */

/** Writes that create a file never follow a symlink at the last component, where the platform can say so. */
const CREATE_FLAGS = constants.O_WRONLY | constants.O_CREAT | constants.O_TRUNC | (constants.O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0);
/** archive.part only ever grows at its end, through this descriptor, and is never followed through a symlink. */
const APPEND_FLAGS = constants.O_WRONLY | constants.O_CREAT | constants.O_APPEND | (constants.O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0);

/** What a chunk's write came to: kept, or truncated back to the stored size because it was short, long or damaged. */
export type ChunkWrite = "kept" | "mismatch";

export interface ImportFilesOptions {
  archivesDir: string;
  workDir: string;
  log: Logger;
  /** Tests only: the free space of import-archives in bytes, in place of statfs. */
  freeBytes?: () => Promise<number>;
  /** Tests only: openWorkFile's device seam, as the media files' storeDevice is. */
  workDevice?: number;
}

/** A name in a folder that is an import id, with the age of the entry itself (never of what a link names). */
export interface AgedId {
  id: string;
  ageMs: number;
}

export function createImportFiles(options: ImportFilesOptions) {
  const archives = archivesLayout(options.archivesDir);
  const work = workLayout(options.workDir);
  const { log } = options;
  const device = options.workDevice === undefined ? {} : { device: options.workDevice };

  /** The import ids among a folder's names, each with the age of its entry; a folder that is not there has none. */
  async function agedIds(dir: string, now: number): Promise<AgedId[]> {
    const names = await readdir(dir).catch(() => [] as string[]);
    const found: AgedId[] = [];
    for (const name of names) {
      if (!isImportId(name)) continue;
      const stats = await lstat(path.join(dir, name)).catch(() => null);
      if (stats) found.push({ id: name, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
    }
    return found;
  }

  /** Creates a file through a descriptor that follows no symlink, writes it whole and flushes it. */
  async function writeWhole(file: string, body: string): Promise<void> {
    const handle = await open(file, CREATE_FLAGS, 0o600);
    try {
      await handle.writeFile(body);
      await handle.sync();
    } finally {
      await handle.close();
    }
  }

  /** Cuts archive.part back to `size` bytes and flushes it. */
  async function truncate(id: string, size: number): Promise<void> {
    const handle = await open(archives.part(id), constants.O_WRONLY | (constants.O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0));
    try {
      await handle.truncate(size);
      await handle.sync();
    } finally {
      await handle.close();
    }
  }

  return {
    archives,
    work,

    /** Creates import-archives' three folders. import-work is the importer's: the API never creates anything there. */
    async prepare(): Promise<void> {
      for (const dir of [archives.jobs, archives.queue, archives.deletions]) await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    },

    /** Free space on import-archives (4.2 step 3, 7.3), which shares a disk with the database. */
    async freeBytes(): Promise<number> {
      if (options.freeBytes) return options.freeBytes();
      const fs = await statfs(archives.root);
      return fs.bavail * fs.bsize;
    },

    /** Milliseconds since the importer's last heartbeat, or null when there is none it may read (4.2 step 3). */
    async heartbeatAge(now: number): Promise<number | null> {
      const beat = await readHeartbeat(work.root, device);
      return beat.ok ? now - beat.value.at : null;
    },

    /** One file of import-work, opened as the protocol says; the caller closes the handle. */
    openWork: (file: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<WorkFileResult> => openWorkFile(work.root, file, maxBytes, device),

    /** A scan's summary.json, at most 64 KiB, parsed as ImportSummary and naming this import. */
    readSummary: (id: string): Promise<ReadResult<ImportSummary>> => readSummary(work.root, id, device),

    /** The folder of an upload, made by its first chunk. */
    ensureJobDir: async (id: string): Promise<void> => {
      await mkdir(archives.jobDir(id), { recursive: true });
    },

    /** The bytes archive.part holds, or null when there is none. The API alone writes import-archives. */
    async partSize(id: string): Promise<number | null> {
      const stats = await lstat(archives.part(id)).catch((err: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => {
        if (err.code === "ENOENT") return null;
        throw err;
      });
      if (stats === null) return null;
      if (!stats.isFile()) throw new Error("import: archive.part is not a regular file");
      return stats.size;
    },

    /** Cuts archive.part back to `size` bytes: the file then holds only whole chunks that passed (7.3). */
    truncatePart: (id: string, size: number): Promise<void> => truncate(id, size),

    /**
     * Appends one chunk to archive.part (7.3). The body is read as it arrives, counted and hashed, and written through a
     * descriptor opened for appending that follows no symlink; one byte over `length` ends the read. `accept`, for the
     * first chunk, sees the first bytes before any of them is kept, and throws to refuse them. A body that is short, long
     * or whose SHA-256 is not `sha256`, and a body that breaks off, leave the file truncated back to `at`, its stored size,
     * and answer "mismatch"; a kept chunk is flushed (fsync) before the answer, so the row only ever counts bytes on disk.
     */
    async appendChunk(id: string, chunk: { at: number; length: number; sha256: string; body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null; accept?: (head: Buffer) => void; headBytes?: number }): Promise<ChunkWrite> {
      const reader = chunk.body?.getReader();
      const first: Uint8Array[] = [];
      let held = 0;
      let ended = !reader;
      const cancel = () => reader?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
      try {
        // The first bytes, only as many as the check needs, before anything is written.
        const wanted = Math.min(chunk.headBytes ?? 0, chunk.length);
        while (reader && chunk.accept && held < wanted) {
          const read = await reader.read();
          if (read.done) {
            ended = true;
            break;
          }
          first.push(read.value);
          held += read.value.byteLength;
        }
      } catch {
        // A body that broke off before its first bytes arrived: nothing was written.
        await cancel();
        return "mismatch";
      }
      try {
        chunk.accept?.(Buffer.concat(first));
      } catch (err) {
        await cancel();
        throw err;
      }

      const handle: FileHandle = await open(archives.part(id), APPEND_FLAGS, 0o600);
      const hasher = createHash("sha256");
      let bytes = 0;
      let outcome: ChunkWrite = "kept";
      // A write that failed (a full disk) is the server's fault, and is thrown on once the file is cut back.
      let failed: unknown = null;
      // The file must be exactly the stored size, which the caller has made it; one that is not is left as it is.
      let sized = true;
      try {
        if ((await handle.stat()).size !== chunk.at) {
          sized = false;
          outcome = "mismatch";
        }
        const write = async (piece: Uint8Array): Promise<boolean> => {
          bytes += piece.byteLength;
          if (bytes > chunk.length) return false;
          hasher.update(piece);
          await handle.appendFile(piece);
          return true;
        };
        let within = outcome === "kept";
        for (const piece of first) if (within) within = await write(piece);
        while (within && reader && !ended) {
          let read: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof reader.read>>;
          try {
            read = await reader.read();
          } catch {
            // The connection was lost: a short body.
            within = false;
            break;
          }
          if (read.done) break;
          within = await write(read.value);
        }
        if (!within || bytes !== chunk.length || hasher.digest("hex") !== chunk.sha256) outcome = "mismatch";
      } catch (err) {
        failed = err;
        outcome = "mismatch";
      }
      try {
        if (outcome === "kept") await handle.sync();
      } finally {
        await handle.close();
      }
      if (outcome === "mismatch") {
        await cancel();
        // Through a descriptor of its own: Windows refuses to truncate through one opened for appending.
        if (sized) await truncate(id, chunk.at);
      }
      if (failed !== null) throw failed;
      return outcome;
    },

    /**
     * The last chunk's files (7.3): archive.part becomes archive, job.json is written for the importer, and last the
     * queue marker, by whose time the importer takes the oldest archive first.
     */
    async completeArchive(id: string, job: JobFile): Promise<void> {
      await rename(archives.part(id), archives.archive(id));
      await writeWhole(archives.job(id), JSON.stringify(job));
      await writeWhole(archives.queued(id), "");
    },

    /** The archive's folder (archive.part or archive, and job.json) and its queue marker go; both may be gone already. */
    async removeArchive(id: string): Promise<void> {
      await rm(archives.jobDir(id), { recursive: true, force: true });
      await rm(archives.queued(id), { force: true });
    },

    /** Asks the importer to delete the work folder of `id` and to stop scanning it: an empty file, delete/<id>. */
    async requestWorkDeletion(id: string): Promise<void> {
      await writeWhole(archives.deletion(id), "");
    },

    /** Withdraws a request the importer has carried out. */
    withdrawWorkDeletion: (id: string): Promise<void> => rm(archives.deletion(id), { force: true }),

    /** Whether the importer still has a work folder (or anything) at jobs/<id> of import-work. */
    async workFolderPresent(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
      return (await lstat(work.jobDir(id)).catch(() => null)) !== null;
    },

    /** The archive folders, queue markers, deletion requests and work folders, each by import id with its age (7.5 step 8). */
    archiveFolders: (now: number) => agedIds(archives.jobs, now),
    queueMarkers: (now: number) => agedIds(archives.queue, now),
    deletionRequests: (now: number) => agedIds(archives.deletions, now),
    workFolders: (now: number) => agedIds(work.jobs, now),

    log,
  };
}

export type ImportFiles = ReturnType<typeof createImportFiles>;
```

### Create `apps/api/src/imports/flows/chunk.ts`

```ts
import { IMPORT_RULES, type ImportSource } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { enforceImportLimit, ImportError, type ImportDeps } from "../context";

/**
 * PUT /api/imports/:id/archive (3b design, section 7.3): one chunk of the archive, appended to archive.part at the
 * offset the import has stored. Every chunk is exactly IMPORT_RULES.chunkBytes but the last, which ends the archive.
 * The refusals, in this order: a malformed header (invalid_request), the account's 600 chunks an hour (rate_limited), an
 * import that is not the caller's or not uploading (not_found, wrong_state), an offset that is not the stored size
 * (wrong_offset, with the stored size, so the app learns where to go on), a length that breaks the rules or runs past the
 * declared size (chunk_too_large), free space under IMPORT_MIN_FREE_BYTES (imports_unavailable). A body that is short,
 * long or damaged leaves the file at the stored size (chunk_mismatch). The first chunk's first bytes must be the
 * declared source's: a zip's local header for X and Mastodon, a CAR's header for Bluesky; gzip's are a Mastodon archive
 * of before 4.2 (tar_gz), anything else not_an_archive, and either ends the upload as failed. The chunk that completes
 * the archive renames it, writes job.json and the queue marker, and moves the import to scanning.
 */

export interface ChunkRequest {
  /** Import-Offset: the byte at which the chunk starts, in decimal. */
  offset: string | undefined;
  /** Content-Length, which the chunk must carry. */
  length: string | undefined;
  /** Import-Chunk-Sha256: the chunk's SHA-256 as 64 lowercase hex. */
  sha256: string | undefined;
  body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null;
}

/** As many first bytes as the checks below read. */
const HEAD_BYTES = 16;
const DECIMAL = /^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,15})$/;
const SHA256 = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;

/** The unsigned varint at the start of `bytes` and its length, as a CAR's header begins; null when it does not end within 9 bytes. */
function varint(bytes: Uint8Array): [number, number] | null {
  let value = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length && i < 9; i++) {
    value += (bytes[i]! & 0x7f) * 2 ** (7 * i);
    if ((bytes[i]! & 0x80) === 0) return [value, i + 1];
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * What an archive's first bytes say for its declared source (7.3): "ok", or the failure the upload ends with. The same
 * reading as the importer's (apps/importer/src/scan.ts and car/reader.ts), which an app cannot import: gzip's two bytes,
 * a zip's local header, a CAR's varint header length within the block cap followed by a CBOR map.
 */
export function firstBytesVerdict(source: ImportSource, head: Uint8Array): "ok" | "tar_gz" | "not_an_archive" {
  if (head.length >= 2 && head[0] === 0x1f && head[1] === 0x8b) return "tar_gz";
  if (source === "bluesky") {
    const read = varint(head);
    if (read === null) return "not_an_archive";
    const [length, used] = read;
    return length > 0 && length <= IMPORT_RULES.carBlockMaxBytes && head.length > used && head[used]! >> 5 === 5 ? "ok" : "not_an_archive";
  }
  return head.length >= 4 && head[0] === 0x50 && head[1] === 0x4b && head[2] === 0x03 && head[3] === 0x04 ? "ok" : "not_an_archive";
}

/** The first bytes refused: the upload ends as failed with this code. */
class FirstBytesRefused extends Error {
  constructor(readonly failure: "tar_gz" | "not_an_archive") {
    super(failure);
  }
}

/** The stored size the app goes on from, in wrong_offset's details. */
const wrongOffset = (receivedBytes: number) => new ImportError("wrong_offset", { details: { receivedBytes } });

export async function receiveChunk(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, id: string, request: ChunkRequest): Promise<{ receivedBytes: number }> {
  if (!DECIMAL.test(request.offset ?? "") || !SHA256.test(request.sha256 ?? "")) throw new ImportError("invalid_request");
  const offset = Number(request.offset);
  const sha256 = request.sha256!;
  // Content-Length is required: a body without it could not be held to the chunk's rules before it is read.
  const length = DECIMAL.test(request.length ?? "") ? Number(request.length) : null;
  await enforceImportLimit(deps, "import-chunk", ownerId);

  const row = await deps.repo.find(id, ownerId);
  if (!row) throw new ImportError("not_found");
  if (row.status !== "uploading") throw new ImportError("wrong_state");
  // One chunk at a time: another one of this import is still on its way in.
  if (deps.inFlight.has(id)) throw wrongOffset(row.receivedBytes);
  deps.inFlight.add(id);
  try {
    const stored = await reconcile(deps, ownerId, row.id, row.receivedBytes, row.declaredBytes);
    if (offset !== stored) throw wrongOffset(stored);
    const end = stored + (length ?? 0);
    if (length === null || length < 1 || length > deps.chunkBytes || end > row.declaredBytes || (length !== deps.chunkBytes && end !== row.declaredBytes)) {
      throw new ImportError("chunk_too_large");
    }
    const free = await deps.files.freeBytes().catch(() => -1);
    if (free < deps.settings.minFreeBytes) {
      deps.log.error({ id, freeBytes: free }, "import: a chunk refused, free space on import-archives is under IMPORT_MIN_FREE_BYTES");
      throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");
    }

    if (stored === 0) await deps.files.ensureJobDir(id);
    const accept =
      stored === 0
        ? (head: Buffer) => {
            const verdict = firstBytesVerdict(row.source, head);
            if (verdict !== "ok") throw new FirstBytesRefused(verdict);
          }
        : undefined;
    let written: "kept" | "mismatch";
    try {
      written = await deps.files.appendChunk(id, { at: stored, length, sha256, body: request.body, accept, headBytes: HEAD_BYTES });
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof FirstBytesRefused) {
        await deps.repo.failUpload(id, ownerId, err.failure);
        await deps.files.removeArchive(id);
        deps.log.info({ id, phase: "failed", failure: err.failure }, "import: the first bytes are not an archive of the source");
        throw new ImportError("not_an_archive");
      }
      deps.log.error({ id, error: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? "write" }, "import: a chunk could not be written");
      throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");
    }
    if (written === "mismatch") throw new ImportError("chunk_mismatch");

    if (end < row.declaredBytes) {
      // A move that lost to a cancel: the chunk on disk passed, and the cancel takes the folder with it.
      if (!(await deps.repo.setReceived(id, ownerId, stored, end))) throw new ImportError("wrong_state");
      return { receivedBytes: end };
    }

    // The last chunk: the archive is complete. The account's key goes into job.json, the importer's one secret (5.4).
    const accountKey = await deps.repo.accountKey(ownerId);
    if (accountKey === null) throw new Error("import: the account has an import but no import key");
    await deps.files.completeArchive(id, { v: 1, id, source: row.source, accountKey, images: row.images, createdAt: row.createdAt.toISOString() });
    if (!(await deps.repo.completeUpload(id, ownerId, stored))) {
      // A cancel came first: the importer must not scan what nobody waits for.
      await deps.files.removeArchive(id);
      await deps.files.requestWorkDeletion(id);
      throw new ImportError("wrong_state");
    }
    deps.log.info({ id, phase: "uploaded", bytes: row.declaredBytes }, "import: the archive is complete and queued");
    return { receivedBytes: row.declaredBytes };
  } finally {
    deps.inFlight.delete(id);
  }
}

/**
 * The file's own size is the truth (7.3): a row behind its file (the process stopped between a chunk's write and its
 * update) takes the file's size, but only up to whole chunks and never the last one, whose request also completes the
 * archive and must come again; the file is cut back to what the row then holds, so a chunk cut short by the stop is sent
 * again. A file shorter than the row has lost bytes nothing can bring back: the upload cannot go on, and expires.
 */
async function reconcile(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, id: string, received: number, declared: number): Promise<number> {
  const size = await deps.files.partSize(id);
  if (size === received || (size === null && received === 0)) return received;
  if (size === null || size < received) {
    deps.log.error({ id, receivedBytes: received, fileBytes: size }, "import: archive.part holds less than its row counts");
    throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");
  }
  const whole = Math.floor(size / deps.chunkBytes) * deps.chunkBytes;
  const lastStart = Math.floor((declared - 1) / deps.chunkBytes) * deps.chunkBytes;
  const taken = Math.max(received, Math.min(whole, lastStart));
  if (size > taken) await deps.files.truncatePart(id, taken);
  if (taken > received) {
    if (!(await deps.repo.setReceived(id, ownerId, received, taken))) throw new ImportError("wrong_state");
    deps.log.warn({ id, receivedBytes: received, takenBytes: taken }, "import: a row behind its file took the file's whole chunks");
  }
  return taken;
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/imports/flows/create.ts`

```ts
import { randomBytes, randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { CreateImportRequest, IMPORT_RULES, type ImportView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { IMPORTER_HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS } from "@korbat/import-protocol";
import { ImportError, type ImportDeps } from "../context";
import { importView } from "../view";

/** A day, the window of the per-address limit (7.6, import-address-day). */
const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000;

/**
 * POST /api/imports (3b design, section 4.2 step 3): creates an import in uploading. Its refusals come cheapest first and
 * in 4.2's order: a declared size over the cap (archive_too_large, before the body's other rules), imports switched off or
 * the source not among IMPORT_SOURCES (imports_unavailable), then, from the one statement that locks the profile row,
 * an account that is not live or is suspended (account_suspended), one younger than seven days or whose address is not
 * verified (import_too_soon), an active import (import_active), three published imports in seven days
 * (import_weekly_limit); then the address's five a day (rate_limited), the site's count of uploads and scans, the
 * importer's heartbeat and the free space for the archive and its scan (imports_unavailable). The last ones run inside
 * the creating transaction, so a refusal rolls the row back, and the address's count is given back for every import that
 * was not created. Nothing is written to a volume but the upload's empty folder, after the commit.
 */
export async function createImport(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, body: unknown, addressKey: string): Promise<ImportView> {
  // The cap first: CreateImportRequest refuses a size over it like any malformed body, and this one has its own words.
  const declared = typeof body === "object" && body !== null ? (body as { bytes?: unknown }).bytes : undefined;
  if (typeof declared === "number" && declared > IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes) throw new ImportError("archive_too_large");
  const parsed = CreateImportRequest.safeParse(body);
  if (!parsed.success) throw new ImportError("invalid_request");
  const { source, bytes } = parsed.data;
  if (!deps.settings.imports || !deps.settings.sources.includes(source)) throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");

  // The address is the auth module's, read before the transaction and judged in 4.2's order inside it.
  const verified = await deps.auth.emailVerified(ownerId);
  const id = randomUUID();
  const bucket = `imports:import-address-day:${addressKey}`;
  let counted = false;
  try {
    await deps.repo.create({ id, ownerId, source, bytes, images: deps.settings.images, verified, maxActive: deps.settings.maxActive, key: randomBytes(IMPORT_RULES.keyBytes) }, async (facts) => {
      if (!facts.live) throw new ImportError("account_suspended");
      if (!facts.aged || !verified) throw new ImportError("import_too_soon");
      if (facts.active) throw new ImportError("import_active");
      if (facts.week >= IMPORT_RULES.importsPerWeek) {
        const wait = facts.weekFreesAt === null ? 1 : Math.ceil((facts.weekFreesAt.getTime() - deps.now().getTime()) / 1000);
        throw new ImportError("import_weekly_limit", { retryAfterSeconds: Math.max(1, wait) });
      }
      let hit: { count: number; resetMs: number };
      try {
        hit = await deps.limits.hit(bucket, DAY_MS);
        counted = true;
      } catch {
        throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");
      }
      if (hit.count > IMPORT_RULES.importsPerAddressDay) throw new ImportError("rate_limited", { retryAfterSeconds: Math.max(1, Math.ceil(hit.resetMs / 1000)) });
      if (facts.site >= deps.settings.maxActive) {
        deps.log.warn({ site: facts.site, maxActive: deps.settings.maxActive }, "import: refused, the site's uploads and scans are at IMPORT_MAX_ACTIVE");
        throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");
      }
      const age = await deps.files.heartbeatAge(deps.now().getTime());
      if (age === null || age >= IMPORTER_HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS) {
        deps.log.error({ ageMs: age }, "import: refused, the importer's heartbeat is missing or stale");
        throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");
      }
      // The archive, the most its scan may write to import-work (7.2), and the floor the owner keeps free.
      const needed = bytes + IMPORT_RULES.scanWriteBytes + deps.settings.minFreeBytes;
      const free = await deps.files.freeBytes().catch(() => -1);
      if (free < needed) {
        deps.log.error({ freeBytes: free, neededBytes: needed }, "import: refused, free space on import-archives is under what an import needs");
        throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");
      }
    });
  } catch (err) {
    // An import that was not created costs the address nothing.
    if (counted) await deps.limits.release(bucket).catch(() => undefined);
    throw err;
  }
  // The upload's folder; its first chunk makes it again if this fails.
  await deps.files.ensureJobDir(id).catch((err: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ id, error: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code }, "import: the upload's folder could not be made yet"));
  deps.log.info({ id, phase: "created", source, bytes }, "import: created");
  const row = await deps.repo.find(id, ownerId);
  if (!row) throw new ImportError("not_found");
  return importView(deps, row);
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/imports/flows/end.ts`

```ts
import type { ImportView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { enforceImportLimit, ImportError, type ImportDeps } from "../context";
import { importView } from "../view";

/**
 * The files of an import that has ended before its posts were chosen, or whose scan the drive has read (3b design,
 * sections 4.8, 6.6 and 7.5): its archive folder and queue marker go at once, and the importer is asked to delete its
 * work folder and to stop scanning it (delete/<id>, which the drive withdraws once it is carried out). Each step is safe
 * to repeat and leaves nothing to undo.
 */
export async function endFiles(deps: Pick<ImportDeps, "files">, id: string): Promise<void> {
  await deps.files.removeArchive(id);
  await deps.files.requestWorkDeletion(id);
}

/**
 * POST /api/imports/:id/cancel (9.2): the person's cancel while the archive uploads, waits for its scan or is previewed;
 * counted in import-act. A suspended account may cancel: it only ends and deletes (8.5).
 */
export async function cancelImport(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, id: string): Promise<ImportView> {
  await enforceImportLimit(deps, "import-act", ownerId);
  if (!(await deps.repo.find(id, ownerId))) throw new ImportError("not_found");
  if (!(await deps.repo.cancel(id, ownerId))) throw new ImportError("wrong_state");
  await endFiles(deps, id);
  deps.log.info({ id, phase: "cancelled" }, "import: cancelled");
  const row = await deps.repo.find(id, ownerId);
  if (!row) throw new ImportError("not_found");
  return importView(deps, row);
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/imports/flows/picks.ts`

```ts
import type { FileHandle } from "node:fs/promises";
import { IMPORT_RULES, ImportPickRequest, MEDIA_MAX_BYTES, type ImportLineView, type ImportPickView, type ImportedPost } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { SAMPLE_MAX_BYTES, isImportMediaFile, readLineAt, readLines } from "@korbat/import-protocol";
import { SNIFF_BYTES, sniffImage } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { enforceImportLimit, ImportError, type ImportDeps } from "../context";
import { latestDate, marksOf, readableLine } from "../intake";
import { pgError, type ImportRow } from "../repo";
import { pickCounts, scanOf } from "../view";

/**
 * The preview's list and the person's picks (3b design, sections 4.4 and 9.2), and the preview's images. Each reads
 * posts.jsonl or one image through openWorkFile, only while the import is ready, from the offsets the intake noted:
 * scan.pages holds every fiftieth offered line's offset, so page n is read from pages[n] up to pages[n + 1], and a line
 * there is shown only by the intake's own rule (readable, at or after fromRef, not already imported).
 */

/** How many readable lines are asked about at once whether the account already imported them. */
const KNOWN_BATCH = 100;

type Ready = { row: ImportRow; scan: NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof scanOf>> };

async function readyImport(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, id: string): Promise<Ready> {
  const row = await deps.repo.find(id, ownerId);
  if (!row) throw new ImportError("not_found");
  const scan = scanOf(row);
  if (row.status !== "ready" || scan === null) throw new ImportError("wrong_state");
  return { row, scan };
}

/** posts.jsonl through openWorkFile; a refusal is logged with its code and answered as the site's (the importer misbehaved). */
async function openPosts(deps: ImportDeps, id: string): Promise<FileHandle> {
  const opened = await deps.files.openWork(deps.files.work.posts(id), IMPORT_RULES.postsFileMaxBytes);
  if (!opened.ok) {
    deps.log.error({ id, code: opened.code }, "import: posts.jsonl was refused");
    throw new ImportError("imports_unavailable");
  }
  return opened.file.handle;
}

/** Which of a line's images open through openWorkFile within 20 MiB: the intake counted the others missing_file. */
async function present(deps: ImportDeps, row: ImportRow, post: ImportedPost): Promise<boolean[]> {
  if (!row.images) return post.media.map(() => false);
  const found: boolean[] = [];
  for (const media of post.media) {
    const opened = await deps.files.openWork(deps.files.work.media(row.id, media.file), MEDIA_MAX_BYTES);
    if (opened.ok) await opened.file.handle.close();
    found.push(opened.ok);
  }
  return found;
}

/** The archive's day of a line, never its second. */
const dayOf = (at: string): string => at.slice(0, 10);

/** GET /api/imports/:id/lines?page=<n>: 50 offered lines of the preview with their marks and picks, and how many pages there are. */
export async function linesPage(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, id: string, page: number): Promise<{ lines: ImportLineView[]; pages: number }> {
  const { row, scan } = await readyImport(deps, ownerId, id);
  const pages = scan.pages.length;
  const from = scan.pages[page];
  if (from === undefined) return { lines: [], pages };
  const latest = latestDate(row.createdAt);
  const handle = await openPosts(deps, id);
  const shown: ImportedPost[] = [];
  try {
    let batch: ImportedPost[] = [];
    const settle = async () => {
      const known = await deps.social.importedKeys(ownerId, batch.map((post) => post.key));
      for (const post of batch) if (!known.has(post.key) && shown.length < IMPORT_RULES.pageLines) shown.push(post);
      batch = [];
    };
    let index: number | null = null;
    // A page reads up to the next page's offset (Task 1's settlement), so its lines are its own.
    for await (const line of readLines(handle, { from, maxBytes: scan.pages[page + 1] ?? IMPORT_RULES.postsFileMaxBytes })) {
      // The first line of a page is an offered line, whose ref is its place in the file; the next ones count from it.
      // A first line that names no ref (the file changed under the intake) leaves the whole page unreadable.
      if (index === null) index = readFirstRef(line.text) ?? Number.NaN;
      const post = readableLine(line.text, index, latest);
      index++;
      if (post === null || post.ref < scan.fromRef) continue;
      batch.push(post);
      if (batch.length >= KNOWN_BATCH) await settle();
      if (shown.length >= IMPORT_RULES.pageLines) break;
    }
    if (batch.length > 0 && shown.length < IMPORT_RULES.pageLines) await settle();
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
  const picks = new Map((await deps.repo.picks(id, shown.map((post) => post.ref))).map((pick) => [pick.ref, pick]));
  const lines: ImportLineView[] = shown.map((post) => ({
    ref: post.ref,
    at: dayOf(post.at),
    kind: post.kind,
    marks: marksOf(post),
    text: post.text,
    media: row.images ? post.media.map(({ file, alt }) => ({ file, alt })) : [],
    leftOut: picks.get(post.ref)?.leftOut ?? false,
    alts: picks.get(post.ref)?.alts ?? [],
  }));
  return { lines, pages };
}

/** The ref a line names, read loosely, for the first line of a page, whose place the intake checked. */
function readFirstRef(text: string | null): number | null {
  if (text === null) return null;
  try {
    const ref = (JSON.parse(text) as { ref?: unknown }).ref;
    return typeof ref === "number" && Number.isInteger(ref) && ref >= 0 && ref < IMPORT_RULES.maxPosts ? ref : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * The offered line `ref`, found from the pages' offsets: the last page whose first line's ref is at most `ref` (a binary
 * search, each step one bounded read), then the line `ref - base` lines further on. Null when no offered line has it.
 */
async function offeredLine(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, ready: Ready, ref: number): Promise<ImportedPost | null> {
  const { row, scan } = ready;
  if (ref < scan.fromRef || scan.pages.length === 0) return null;
  const latest = latestDate(row.createdAt);
  const handle = await openPosts(deps, row.id);
  try {
    const firstRef = async (page: number) => readFirstRef(await readLineAt(handle, scan.pages[page]!, SAMPLE_MAX_BYTES));
    let low = 0;
    let high = scan.pages.length - 1;
    let base: number | null = null;
    let at = -1;
    while (low <= high) {
      const middle = (low + high) >> 1;
      const first = await firstRef(middle);
      if (first === null) return null;
      if (first <= ref) {
        base = first;
        at = middle;
        low = middle + 1;
      } else {
        high = middle - 1;
      }
    }
    if (base === null) return null;
    let index = base;
    for await (const line of readLines(handle, { from: scan.pages[at]!, maxBytes: scan.pages[at + 1] ?? IMPORT_RULES.postsFileMaxBytes, maxLines: ref - base + 1 })) {
      if (index === ref) {
        const post = readableLine(line.text, index, latest);
        if (post === null) return null;
        const known = await deps.social.importedKeys(ownerId, [post.key]);
        return known.has(post.key) ? null : post;
      }
      index++;
    }
    return null;
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

/**
 * PUT /api/imports/:id/lines/:ref (9.2): leaves an offered line out or brings it back, and gives each of its images
 * that its source left without a description one of the person's (decision 20), saved at once in import_picks with the
 * line's month, marks and described images; counted in import-pick. A description for an image the source described,
 * or for an image a line does not have, is refused (invalid_request), and while images are off a line takes none.
 */
export async function pickLine(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, id: string, ref: number, body: unknown): Promise<ImportPickView> {
  const parsed = ImportPickRequest.safeParse(body);
  if (!parsed.success) throw new ImportError("invalid_request");
  await enforceImportLimit(deps, "import-pick", ownerId);
  const ready = await readyImport(deps, ownerId, id);
  const post = await offeredLine(deps, ownerId, ready, ref);
  if (post === null) throw new ImportError("not_found");
  const { leftOut, alts } = parsed.data;
  const there = await present(deps, ready.row, post);
  for (const [position, alt] of alts.entries()) {
    if (alt === null) continue;
    if (!there[position] || post.media[position]!.alt !== null) throw new ImportError("invalid_request");
  }
  const described = post.media.filter((media, position) => there[position] && media.alt !== null).length;
  const kept = alts.some((alt) => alt !== null) ? alts : null;
  try {
    await deps.repo.upsertPick(id, { ref, leftOut, alts: kept, month: post.at.slice(0, 7), marks: marksOf(post), described });
  } catch (err) {
    // import_picks_guard: the import left ready meanwhile (a confirmation, a cancel, the expiry).
    if (pgError(err)?.code === "42501") throw new ImportError("wrong_state");
    throw err;
  }
  return { ref, leftOut, alts: kept ?? [], picks: pickCounts(await deps.repo.picks(id)) };
}

/** The image types the preview shows (9.2): the sniffed format decides, never the name. */
const SHOWN = { jpeg: "image/jpeg", png: "image/png", webp: "image/webp" } as const;

/**
 * GET /api/imports/:id/media/:file (9.2): one image of the preview, the owner's only, while the import is ready and brings
 * images, opened through openWorkFile within 20 MiB and sniffed as JPEG, PNG or WebP; anything else is not_found. The
 * caller streams it from the handle and closes it.
 */
export async function mediaFile(deps: ImportDeps, ownerId: string, id: string, file: string): Promise<{ handle: FileHandle; size: number; type: string }> {
  if (!isImportMediaFile(file)) throw new ImportError("not_found");
  const { row } = await readyImport(deps, ownerId, id);
  if (!row.images) throw new ImportError("not_found");
  const opened = await deps.files.openWork(deps.files.work.media(id, file), MEDIA_MAX_BYTES);
  if (!opened.ok) {
    if (opened.code !== "missing") deps.log.warn({ id, code: opened.code }, "import: an image of the preview was refused");
    throw new ImportError("not_found");
  }
  const { handle, size } = opened.file;
  const head = Buffer.alloc(SNIFF_BYTES);
  const { bytesRead } = await handle.read(head, 0, SNIFF_BYTES, 0);
  const sniffed = sniffImage(head.subarray(0, bytesRead));
  const type = sniffed.kind === "image" && sniffed.format in SHOWN ? SHOWN[sniffed.format as keyof typeof SHOWN] : null;
  if (type === null) {
    await handle.close();
    throw new ImportError("not_found");
  }
  return { handle, size, type };
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/imports/index.ts`

```ts
/**
 * The only file outside `src/imports/` may import. Everything else in the module is private and the architecture test
 * fails the build if another file reaches into it (3b design, section 9.1).
 */
import type { MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { IMPORT_RULES, type ImportSource } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";
import type { AuthForImports } from "../auth";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import type { JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { SocialForImports } from "../social";
import type { ImportDeps, ImportSettings } from "./context";
import { createDriveJob, driveRound, type DriveOptions } from "./drive";
import { createImportFiles } from "./files";
import { createImportRepo } from "./repo";
import { importRoutes } from "./routes";

export { ImportError } from "./context";
export type { ImportDeps, ImportErrorKind, ImportSettings } from "./context";
export type { DriveReport } from "./drive";
export type { ImportList } from "./routes";

/** The owner's settings of section 7.7, as config.ts read and checked them. */
export function importSettingsFrom(config: Pick<Config, "IMPORTS" | "IMPORT_IMAGES" | "IMPORT_SOURCES" | "IMPORT_MAX_ACTIVE" | "IMPORT_IMAGES_PER_HOUR" | "IMPORT_MIN_FREE_BYTES">): ImportSettings {
  return {
    imports: config.IMPORTS === "on",
    images: config.IMPORT_IMAGES === "on",
    sources: config.IMPORT_SOURCES as readonly ImportSource[],
    maxActive: config.IMPORT_MAX_ACTIVE,
    imagesPerHour: config.IMPORT_IMAGES_PER_HOUR,
    minFreeBytes: config.IMPORT_MIN_FREE_BYTES,
  };
}

export interface CreateImportsOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** import-archives, which the API writes and the importer only reads, and import-work, which the API only reads. */
  archivesDir: string;
  workDir: string;
  settings: ImportSettings;
  /** The auth module's interface: whether an account's address is verified (4.2 step 3). */
  auth: AuthForImports;
  /** The social module's interface: which lines the account already imported (7.5 step 2). */
  social: SocialForImports;
  /** The store every limit counts in. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;
  /** Tests only: the free space of import-archives, openWorkFile's device, and a smaller chunk. */
  freeBytes?: () => Promise<number>;
  workDevice?: number;
  chunkBytes?: number;
}

export function createImports(options: CreateImportsOptions) {
  const deps: ImportDeps = {
    repo: createImportRepo(options.apiDb),
    files: createImportFiles({ archivesDir: options.archivesDir, workDir: options.workDir, log: options.logger, freeBytes: options.freeBytes, workDevice: options.workDevice }),
    auth: options.auth,
    social: options.social,
    limits: options.rateLimitStore,
    settings: options.settings,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
    chunkBytes: options.chunkBytes ?? IMPORT_RULES.chunkBytes,
    inFlight: new Set(),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    /** Mounted at /api/imports after the session's resolution. */
    routes: importRoutes(deps, options.requireSession),
    /** Creates import-archives' folders. Call once before serving. */
    prepare: () => deps.files.prepare(),
    /** One round of import-drive at the given time. The server runs it on a timer; tests call it directly. */
    drive: (now: Date, driveOptions: DriveOptions) => driveRound(deps, now, driveOptions),
    /** Starts import-drive under the shared job lock, a round every five seconds, and returns the function that stops it. */
    startJobs: (lock: JobLock) => createDriveJob(deps, lock).start(),
  };
}

export type Imports = ReturnType<typeof createImports>;
```

### Create `apps/api/src/imports/intake.ts`

```ts
import { IMPORT_MARKS, IMPORT_RULES, MEDIA_MAX_BYTES, postLength, type ImportImageSkip, type ImportScanFacts, type ImportSkipReason, type ImportSummary, type ImportedPost } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { LINE_MAX_BYTES, POSTS_MAX_BYTES, POSTS_MAX_LINES, parsePostLine, readLines, type WorkFileRefusal } from "@korbat/import-protocol";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { ImportFiles } from "./files";

/**
 * The intake (3b design, section 7.5 step 2): what the API makes of a scan once its summary says "scanned". It reads
 * posts.jsonl line by line through openWorkFile, each line at most 256 KiB and parsed with the contracts' ImportedPost,
 * and keeps per line only a few numbers in typed arrays (its offset, month, marks and images) and its key, so 50,000
 * lines of up to 1 GiB cost a few megabytes. A line is readable when it parses and its ref is its place in the file
 * (refs run 0, 1, 2 in order); any other line is counted unreadable and is in no table. Each image a readable line names
 * must open through openWorkFile within 20 MiB, or it is counted missing_file and left out of the line; a line dated
 * outside the range the importer keeps (5.4: from 2006-03-21 to a day after the import's creation) is unreadable too, so
 * no hostile file can grow the month table past what the row holds. Then, in batches
 * of a thousand keys, the lines whose key the account's posts already carry are counted already_imported; for an
 * account younger than 30 days every offered line but the newest thousand is counted new_account_cap, and fromRef names
 * the lowest ref that may be published. What is left is offered: its month table, the three newest lines as samples and
 * every fiftieth line's offset as the preview's pages. Nothing of a line's text is kept or logged.
 */

/** A scanned summary: the importer's counts, which the intake adds its own to. */
export type ScannedSummary = Extract<ImportSummary, { status: "scanned" }>;

/** The caps of 7.5 step 2 and decision 21; tests give smaller ones. */
export interface IntakeCaps {
  lines: number;
  bytes: number;
  lineBytes: number;
  newAccountPosts: number;
  images: number;
}

const CAPS: IntakeCaps = {
  lines: POSTS_MAX_LINES,
  bytes: POSTS_MAX_BYTES,
  lineBytes: LINE_MAX_BYTES,
  newAccountPosts: IMPORT_RULES.newAccountMaxPosts,
  images: IMPORT_RULES.maxImages,
};

export interface IntakeOptions {
  id: string;
  summary: ScannedSummary;
  /** Whether the import brings images (its row's images, which job.json said too). */
  images: boolean;
  /** When the import was created, from which the latest date a line may carry counts (5.4). */
  createdAt: Date;
  /** The account is younger than 30 days (decision 21). */
  young: boolean;
  /** The social module's read: which of these keys the account's posts carry now (at most a thousand a call). */
  known: (keys: readonly string[]) => Promise<ReadonlySet<string>>;
  files: Pick<ImportFiles, "openWork" | "work">;
  log: Logger;
  caps?: Partial<IntakeCaps>;
}

export type IntakeResult = { ok: true; scan: ImportScanFacts } | { ok: false; code: WorkFileRefusal | "invalid" };

/** A line's marks, as IMPORT_MARKS' bits: reply, long (over shortenTo code points), warning, protected. */
export function marksOf(post: Pick<ImportedPost, "kind" | "text" | "warning" | "protected">): number {
  const bit = (mark: (typeof IMPORT_MARKS)[number]) => 1 << IMPORT_MARKS.indexOf(mark);
  let marks = 0;
  if (post.kind === "reply") marks |= bit("reply");
  if (postLength(post.text) > IMPORT_RULES.shortenTo) marks |= bit("long");
  if (post.warning) marks |= bit("warning");
  if (post.protected) marks |= bit("protected");
  return marks;
}

/** The latest date a line of an import created at `createdAt` may carry (5.4), in the lines' own format. */
export const latestDate = (createdAt: Date): string => new Date(createdAt.getTime() + IMPORT_RULES.futureDays * 86_400_000).toISOString().replace(/[.][0-9]+Z$/, "Z");
const EARLIEST = `${IMPORT_RULES.earliestDate}T00:00:00Z`;

/**
 * A line as the intake reads it: the ImportedPost it holds when it parses, its ref is its place in the file and its date
 * is within the range the importer keeps; null for any other line, which is unreadable. The lines and picks routes read
 * a line by the same rule, so they show exactly the lines the intake offered. Dates are whole seconds of UTC in one
 * format, so their text compares as their time does.
 */
export function readableLine(text: string | null, index: number, latest: string): ImportedPost | null {
  const post = text === null ? null : parsePostLine(text);
  return post === null || post.ref !== index || post.at < EARLIEST || post.at > latest ? null : post;
}

/** The month of a line's date, YYYY-MM, as one number (YYYYMM), and back. */
const monthNumber = (at: string): number => Number(at.slice(0, 4)) * 100 + Number(at.slice(5, 7));
const monthText = (n: number): string => `${String(Math.floor(n / 100)).padStart(4, "0")}-${String(n % 100).padStart(2, "0")}`;

/** The set bits of a small number. */
const bits = (n: number): number => {
  let count = 0;
  for (let v = n; v > 0; v >>= 1) count += v & 1;
  return count;
};

/** Adds one count to a partial record of reasons, keeping only the reasons that have one. */
function add<K extends string>(record: Partial<Record<K, number>>, key: K, by: number): void {
  if (by > 0) record[key] = (record[key] ?? 0) + by;
}

const READABLE = 1;
const KNOWN = 2;

export async function runIntake(options: IntakeOptions): Promise<IntakeResult> {
  const caps = { ...CAPS, ...options.caps };
  const { files, id, log } = options;
  const opened = await files.openWork(files.work.posts(id), caps.bytes);
  if (!opened.ok) return { ok: false, code: opened.code };

  const offsets = new Float64Array(caps.lines);
  const state = new Uint8Array(caps.lines);
  const months = new Int32Array(caps.lines);
  const marks = new Uint8Array(caps.lines);
  const imageCount = new Uint8Array(caps.lines);
  // The positions, among the images kept, of those without a source's description.
  const undescribed = new Uint8Array(caps.lines);
  const keys: string[] = [];
  const skipped: Partial<Record<ImportSkipReason, number>> = {};
  const imagesSkipped: Partial<Record<ImportImageSkip, number>> = {};
  const refused: Partial<Record<string, number>> = {};
  let lines = 0;
  let unreadable = 0;
  const latest = latestDate(options.createdAt);
  try {
    for await (const line of readLines(opened.file.handle, { maxLines: caps.lines, maxBytes: caps.bytes, lineMaxBytes: caps.lineBytes })) {
      const ref = lines++;
      offsets[ref] = line.offset;
      keys.push("");
      const post = readableLine(line.text, ref, latest);
      if (post === null) {
        unreadable++;
        continue;
      }
      state[ref] = READABLE;
      keys[ref] = post.key;
      months[ref] = monthNumber(post.at);
      marks[ref] = marksOf(post);
      if (post.media.length > 0 && !options.images) {
        // An importer told that images are off writes none; whatever a line names then is not imported.
        add(imagesSkipped, "images_off", post.media.length);
        continue;
      }
      let kept = 0;
      let mask = 0;
      for (const media of post.media) {
        const image = await files.openWork(files.work.media(id, media.file), MEDIA_MAX_BYTES);
        if (!image.ok) {
          add(imagesSkipped, "missing_file", 1);
          add(refused, image.code, 1);
          continue;
        }
        await image.file.handle.close();
        if (media.alt === null) mask |= 1 << kept;
        kept++;
      }
      imageCount[ref] = kept;
      undescribed[ref] = mask;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    log.error({ id, phase: "intake", error: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? "read" }, "import: posts.jsonl could not be read");
    return { ok: false, code: "error" };
  } finally {
    await opened.file.handle.close();
  }
  if (Object.keys(refused).length > 0) log.warn({ id, phase: "intake", refused }, "import: images the importer named were refused (missing_file)");

  // Lines whose key the account's posts carry now, asked in batches.
  let known = 0;
  for (let from = 0; from < lines; from += IMPORT_RULES.keyBatch) {
    const batch: number[] = [];
    for (let ref = from; ref < Math.min(lines, from + IMPORT_RULES.keyBatch); ref++) if (state[ref] === READABLE) batch.push(ref);
    if (batch.length === 0) continue;
    const found = await options.known(batch.map((ref) => keys[ref]!));
    for (const ref of batch) {
      if (found.has(keys[ref]!)) {
        state[ref] = KNOWN;
        known++;
      }
    }
  }

  // The lines offered, oldest first; a young account's newest thousand of them only.
  let offered: number[] = [];
  for (let ref = 0; ref < lines; ref++) if (state[ref] === READABLE) offered.push(ref);
  let capped = 0;
  if (options.young && offered.length > caps.newAccountPosts) {
    capped = offered.length - caps.newAccountPosts;
    offered = offered.slice(capped);
  }
  const fromRef = options.young && offered.length > 0 ? offered[0]! : 0;

  // Images, newest posts first, at most the cap; a line's images beyond it are its last ones.
  const table = new Map<number, Map<number, [number, number, number]>>();
  let images = 0;
  let overImages = 0;
  for (let i = offered.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const ref = offered[i]!;
    const count = Math.min(imageCount[ref]!, Math.max(0, caps.images - images));
    overImages += imageCount[ref]! - count;
    images += count;
    const groups = table.get(months[ref]!) ?? new Map<number, [number, number, number]>();
    table.set(months[ref]!, groups);
    const group = groups.get(marks[ref]!) ?? [0, 0, 0];
    groups.set(marks[ref]!, group);
    group[0] += 1;
    group[1] += count;
    group[2] += bits(undescribed[ref]! & ((1 << count) - 1));
  }

  add(skipped, "unreadable", unreadable);
  add(skipped, "already_imported", known);
  add(skipped, "new_account_cap", capped);
  add(imagesSkipped, "over_image_cap", overImages);
  const { v: _v, id: _id, status: _status, ...counts } = options.summary;
  for (const [reason, count] of Object.entries(counts.skipped)) add(skipped, reason as ImportSkipReason, count ?? 0);
  for (const [reason, count] of Object.entries(counts.imagesSkipped)) add(imagesSkipped, reason as ImportImageSkip, count ?? 0);

  const sorted = [...table.keys()].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const pages: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < offered.length && pages.length < IMPORT_RULES.maxPages; i += IMPORT_RULES.pageLines) pages.push(offsets[offered[i]!]!);
  const scan = {
    ...counts,
    posts: offered.length,
    images,
    skipped,
    imagesSkipped,
    months: sorted.map((month) => ({
      month: monthText(month),
      groups: [...table.get(month)!.entries()].sort(([a], [b]) => a - b).map(([group, [posts, withImages, without]]) => [group, posts, withImages, without] as [number, number, number, number]),
    })),
    first: sorted.length > 0 ? monthText(sorted[0]!) : null,
    last: sorted.length > 0 ? monthText(sorted.at(-1)!) : null,
    fromRef,
    samples: offered.slice(-IMPORT_RULES.samples).reverse().map((ref) => ({ ref, offset: offsets[ref]! })),
    pages,
  } satisfies ImportScanFacts;
  log.info({ id, phase: "intake", lines, offered: offered.length, unreadable, known, capped, images }, "import: intake done");
  return { ok: true, scan };
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/imports/repo.ts`

```ts
import { sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import { IMPORT_RULES, type ImportFailure, type ImportScanFacts, type ImportSource, type ImportStatus } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { WRITE_CLOCK, closingJudgment, liveNotSuspended } from "../lib/standing";
import { ImportError } from "./context";

/**
 * Every statement on import_jobs, import_picks and import_keys (3b design, sections 6.1 and 9.1), on the korbat_api pool.
 * The triggers of migration 0043 judge each write: import_jobs_insert forces a new import's columns, import_jobs_guard
 * lets each column change only by the move of section 4.1 that names it, and import_picks_guard takes a pick only while
 * its import is ready. Every move below is one UPDATE that names the state it leaves, so a move that lost a race to
 * another (a cancel and the drive, two requests of one upload) changes nothing and is answered as such.
 */

/** The five active states of 4.1, which import_jobs_one_active counts. */
const ACTIVE = sql`('uploading', 'scanning', 'ready', 'preparing', 'publishing')`;
/** The states in which an import has ended for good, or is being removed: its picks are of no further use (7.5 step 7). */
const ENDED = sql`('done', 'stopped', 'undoing', 'undone', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'expired')`;

/** The columns an import's view and its flows read, with bigint and date columns in forms the driver hands over as they are. */
const COLUMNS = sql`j.id, j.owner_id, j.source::text as source, j.status::text as status, j.declared_bytes::float8 as declared_bytes,
  j.received_bytes::float8 as received_bytes, j.created_at, j.uploaded_at, j.scanned_at, j.confirmed_at, j.ended_at, j.failure,
  j.stop_reason, j.staff_rule_id, to_char(j.refused_at_original, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as refused_at_original, j.refused_words, j.scan,
  j.choice, j.posts_published, j.images_kept, j.images_left_out, j.posts_removed, j.images`;

/**
 * The move out of ready (whichever it is) keeps the counts and fromRef and leaves the month table, the samples, the pages
 * and the count of posts skipped as not public behind (decision 25), as import_jobs_guard requires of it.
 */
const CUT_SCAN = sql`jsonb_set(j.scan || jsonb_build_object('months', '[]'::jsonb, 'samples', '[]'::jsonb, 'pages', '[]'::jsonb),
  '{skipped}', coalesce(j.scan -> 'skipped', '{}'::jsonb) - 'not_public')`;

/** A fixed key of pg_advisory_xact_lock: every creation takes it, so the site's count of active uploads is read and kept by one at a time (4.2 step 3). */
const SITE_LOCK = sql`hashtext('korbat:import_jobs:site_active')`;

export interface ImportRow {
  id: string;
  ownerId: string;
  source: ImportSource;
  status: ImportStatus;
  declaredBytes: number;
  receivedBytes: number;
  createdAt: Date;
  uploadedAt: Date | null;
  scannedAt: Date | null;
  confirmedAt: Date | null;
  endedAt: Date | null;
  failure: ImportFailure | null;
  stopReason: string | null;
  staffRuleId: string | null;
  refusedAtOriginal: string | null;
  refusedWords: string | null;
  /** ImportScanFacts as the drive wrote it; the view parses it before it shows a member. */
  scan: unknown;
  choice: unknown;
  postsPublished: number;
  imagesKept: number;
  imagesLeftOut: number;
  postsRemoved: number;
  /** Whether the import brings images, decided at its creation (migration 0046). */
  images: boolean;
}

interface RawRow {
  id: string;
  owner_id: string;
  source: ImportSource;
  status: ImportStatus;
  declared_bytes: number;
  received_bytes: number;
  created_at: Date | string;
  uploaded_at: Date | string | null;
  scanned_at: Date | string | null;
  confirmed_at: Date | string | null;
  ended_at: Date | string | null;
  failure: ImportFailure | null;
  stop_reason: string | null;
  staff_rule_id: string | null;
  refused_at_original: string | null;
  refused_words: string | null;
  scan: unknown;
  choice: unknown;
  posts_published: number;
  images_kept: number;
  images_left_out: number;
  posts_removed: number;
  images: boolean;
}

const time = (value: Date | string | null): Date | null => (value === null ? null : new Date(value));

function toRow(raw: RawRow): ImportRow {
  return {
    id: raw.id,
    ownerId: raw.owner_id,
    source: raw.source,
    status: raw.status,
    declaredBytes: Number(raw.declared_bytes),
    receivedBytes: Number(raw.received_bytes),
    createdAt: new Date(raw.created_at),
    uploadedAt: time(raw.uploaded_at),
    scannedAt: time(raw.scanned_at),
    confirmedAt: time(raw.confirmed_at),
    endedAt: time(raw.ended_at),
    failure: raw.failure,
    stopReason: raw.stop_reason,
    staffRuleId: raw.staff_rule_id,
    refusedAtOriginal: raw.refused_at_original,
    refusedWords: raw.refused_words,
    scan: raw.scan,
    choice: raw.choice,
    postsPublished: raw.posts_published,
    imagesKept: raw.images_kept,
    imagesLeftOut: raw.images_left_out,
    postsRemoved: raw.posts_removed,
    images: raw.images,
  };
}

/** What the creating statement read, in the order 4.2 step 3 answers its refusals. */
export interface CreateFacts {
  /** The profile row exists, is not deleted and its suspension does not run, by 3e's predicate in the locking statement. */
  live: boolean;
  /** The profile is at least minAccountAgeDays old. */
  aged: boolean;
  /** The account has an import in an active state. */
  active: boolean;
  /** Published imports confirmed in the last seven days, and when the oldest of them leaves the window. */
  week: number;
  weekFreesAt: Date | null;
  /** Imports in uploading or scanning on the site, read under the site's lock. */
  site: number;
  /** The row was inserted. */
  created: boolean;
}

export interface CreateInput {
  id: string;
  ownerId: string;
  source: ImportSource;
  bytes: number;
  images: boolean;
  /** The auth module's answer: the account's address was verified (4.2 step 3). */
  verified: boolean;
  maxActive: number;
  /** A fresh account import key of 32 random bytes, kept only when the account has none (5.4). */
  key: Buffer;
}

/** One pick as import_picks holds it, with the line's facts of migration 0046. */
export interface PickRow {
  ref: number;
  leftOut: boolean;
  alts: (string | null)[] | null;
  month: string;
  marks: number;
  described: number;
}

/** SQLSTATE and constraint of a database error, through drizzle's wrapping of the driver's error. */
export function pgError(err: unknown): { code: string; constraint: string | null; message: string } | null {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    const code = (current as { code?: unknown }).code;
    if (typeof current === "object" && typeof code === "string" && /^[0-9A-Z]{5}$/.test(code)) {
      const found = current as { constraint_name?: unknown; constraint?: unknown; message?: unknown };
      const constraint = typeof found.constraint_name === "string" ? found.constraint_name : typeof found.constraint === "string" ? found.constraint : null;
      return { code, constraint, message: typeof found.message === "string" ? found.message : "" };
    }
    current = (current as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  }
  return null;
}

export function createImportRepo(db: Db) {
  const rows = async <T>(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">, query: SQL): Promise<T[]> => (await q.execute(query)) as unknown as T[];
  const ids = async (query: SQL): Promise<string[]> => (await rows<{ id: string }>(db, query)).map((row) => row.id);

  return {
    /**
     * Creates an import (4.2 step 3, 8.5) in one transaction: the site's lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock on a fixed key, so
     * the count of uploads and scans on the site cannot be passed by two creations at once), then one statement that locks
     * the profile row FOR KEY SHARE, judges it by 3e's predicate by the clock, reads the account's age, its active import,
     * its published imports of the week and the site's count, and inserts the row only when every one allows it. `judge`
     * runs next, inside the transaction, on what the statement read: it throws the refusal in 4.2's order (and makes the
     * checks that are not the database's: the address's limit, the importer's heartbeat, the free space), which rolls
     * the insert back. Then the account's import key, made at its first import and never replaced, and last the closing
     * judgment of the owner (3e's review), which refuses account_suspended for a start that came while it waited.
     */
    async create(input: CreateInput, judge: (facts: CreateFacts) => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
      try {
        await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
          await tx.execute(sql`select pg_advisory_xact_lock(${SITE_LOCK})`);
          const [found] = await rows<{
            live: boolean;
            aged: boolean;
            active: boolean;
            week: number;
            week_frees_at: Date | string | null;
            site: number;
            created: boolean;
          }>(
            tx,
            sql`
            with me as (
              select p.id, p.created_at, ${liveNotSuspended("p", WRITE_CLOCK)} as live
                from profiles p where p.id = ${input.ownerId}::uuid for key share of p
            ), facts as (
              select me.id, me.live,
                     me.created_at <= clock_timestamp() - make_interval(days => ${IMPORT_RULES.minAccountAgeDays}::int) as aged,
                     exists (select 1 from import_jobs j where j.owner_id = me.id and j.status in ${ACTIVE}) as active,
                     (select count(*)::int from import_jobs j
                       where j.owner_id = me.id and j.confirmed_at > clock_timestamp() - interval '7 days' and j.posts_published > 0) as week,
                     (select min(j.confirmed_at) + interval '7 days' from import_jobs j
                       where j.owner_id = me.id and j.confirmed_at > clock_timestamp() - interval '7 days' and j.posts_published > 0) as week_frees_at,
                     (select count(*)::int from import_jobs j where j.status in ('uploading', 'scanning')) as site
                from me
            ), inserted as (
              insert into import_jobs (id, owner_id, source, declared_bytes, images)
              select ${input.id}::uuid, f.id, ${input.source}::import_source, ${input.bytes}::bigint, ${input.images}
                from facts f
               where f.live and f.aged and ${input.verified} and not f.active and f.week < ${IMPORT_RULES.importsPerWeek}::int and f.site < ${input.maxActive}::int
              returning id
            )
            select f.live, f.aged, f.active, f.week, f.week_frees_at, f.site, exists (select 1 from inserted) as created from facts f`,
          );
          const facts: CreateFacts = found
            ? { live: found.live, aged: found.aged, active: found.active, week: found.week, weekFreesAt: time(found.week_frees_at), site: found.site, created: found.created }
            : { live: false, aged: false, active: false, week: 0, weekFreesAt: null, site: 0, created: false };
          await judge(facts);
          if (!facts.created) throw new Error("import: the create statement inserted nothing and no refusal answered it");
          await tx.execute(sql`insert into import_keys (owner_id, key) values (${input.ownerId}::uuid, ${input.key}::bytea) on conflict (owner_id) do nothing`);
          const judged = await closingJudgment(tx, input.ownerId);
          if (!judged || judged.deleted || judged.suspended) throw new ImportError("account_suspended");
        });
      } catch (err) {
        // A second creation of the account that the statement could not see (it would have waited on the site's lock):
        // the unique index answers it.
        if (pgError(err)?.constraint === "import_jobs_one_active") throw new ImportError("import_active");
        throw err;
      }
    },

    /** The account's import, or null for an import of anyone else or none. */
    async find(id: string, ownerId: string): Promise<ImportRow | null> {
      const [raw] = await rows<RawRow>(db, sql`select ${COLUMNS} from import_jobs j where j.id = ${id}::uuid and j.owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid`);
      return raw ? toRow(raw) : null;
    },

    /** The account's imports, newest first, at most `limit`. */
    async list(ownerId: string, limit: number): Promise<ImportRow[]> {
      const found = await rows<RawRow>(db, sql`select ${COLUMNS} from import_jobs j where j.owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid order by j.created_at desc, j.id desc limit ${limit}::int`);
      return found.map(toRow);
    },

    /** The account's import key (5.4), as 64 lowercase hex, for job.json; null when it has none. */
    async accountKey(ownerId: string): Promise<string | null> {
      const [row] = await rows<{ key: string }>(db, sql`select encode(k.key, 'hex') as key from import_keys k where k.owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid`);
      return row?.key ?? null;
    },

    /**
     * The stored size of an upload moves from `from` to `to` in one statement that requires the old value (7.3): of two
     * requests racing for one offset only one can win. False when the row was not at `from` or no longer uploading.
     */
    async setReceived(id: string, ownerId: string, from: number, to: number): Promise<boolean> {
      const done = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        db,
        sql`update import_jobs j set received_bytes = ${to}::bigint
             where j.id = ${id}::uuid and j.owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid and j.status = 'uploading' and j.received_bytes = ${from}::bigint returning j.id`,
      );
      return done.length === 1;
    },

    /** The last chunk's move: uploading to scanning, the whole archive stored, uploaded_at (7.3). */
    async completeUpload(id: string, ownerId: string, from: number): Promise<boolean> {
      const done = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        db,
        sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'scanning', received_bytes = j.declared_bytes, uploaded_at = clock_timestamp()
             where j.id = ${id}::uuid and j.owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid and j.status = 'uploading' and j.received_bytes = ${from}::bigint returning j.id`,
      );
      return done.length === 1;
    },

    /** The first chunk is not an archive of the source (7.3): the upload ends as failed with its code. */
    async failUpload(id: string, ownerId: string, failure: "tar_gz" | "not_an_archive"): Promise<boolean> {
      const done = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        db,
        sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'failed', failure = ${failure}, ended_at = clock_timestamp()
             where j.id = ${id}::uuid and j.owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid and j.status = 'uploading' returning j.id`,
      );
      return done.length === 1;
    },

    /**
     * The person's cancel (9.2) from uploading, scanning or ready, in one statement: out of scanning it sets scanned_at,
     * out of ready it cuts the scan down (decision 25), as the guard requires of each. False when the import is in no
     * state a cancel leaves.
     */
    async cancel(id: string, ownerId: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const done = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        db,
        sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'cancelled', ended_at = clock_timestamp(),
                   scanned_at = case when j.status = 'scanning' then clock_timestamp() else j.scanned_at end,
                   scan = case when j.status = 'ready' then ${CUT_SCAN} else j.scan end
             where j.id = ${id}::uuid and j.owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid and j.status in ('uploading', 'scanning', 'ready') returning j.id`,
      );
      return done.length === 1;
    },

    /** Imports waiting for their scan, with what the intake needs: whether images are on, its creation and when the owner's profile was made. */
    async scanning(): Promise<{ id: string; ownerId: string; images: boolean; createdAt: Date; ownerCreatedAt: Date }[]> {
      const found = await rows<{ id: string; owner_id: string; images: boolean; created_at: Date | string; owner_created_at: Date | string }>(
        db,
        sql`select j.id, j.owner_id, j.images, j.created_at, p.created_at as owner_created_at
              from import_jobs j join profiles p on p.id = j.owner_id where j.status = 'scanning' order by j.created_at, j.id`,
      );
      return found.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, ownerId: row.owner_id, images: row.images, createdAt: new Date(row.created_at), ownerCreatedAt: new Date(row.owner_created_at) }));
    },

    /** A scan's failure (7.5 step 1): scanning to failed, with its code. False when the import left scanning meanwhile. */
    async failScan(id: string, failure: ImportFailure, now: Date): Promise<boolean> {
      const done = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        db,
        sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'failed', failure = ${failure}, scanned_at = ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz, ended_at = ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz
             where j.id = ${id}::uuid and j.status = 'scanning' returning j.id`,
      );
      return done.length === 1;
    },

    /** The intake's end (7.5 step 2): scanning to ready, with its numbers. False when the import left scanning meanwhile. */
    async toReady(id: string, scan: ImportScanFacts, now: Date): Promise<boolean> {
      const done = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        db,
        sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'ready', scan = ${JSON.stringify(scan)}::jsonb, scanned_at = ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz
             where j.id = ${id}::uuid and j.status = 'scanning' returning j.id`,
      );
      return done.length === 1;
    },

    /** 4.8: an upload not complete 24 hours after its creation expires. The ids, whose parts go. */
    expireUploads: (now: Date) =>
      ids(sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'expired', ended_at = ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz
               where j.status = 'uploading' and j.created_at <= ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz - make_interval(hours => ${IMPORT_RULES.archiveHours}::int) returning j.id`),

    /**
     * 4.8: a scan not done 45 minutes after the upload ended, or 24 hours after the import was created if that is sooner,
     * fails as scan_timed_out. The ids, whose archive and work folder go.
     */
    timeOutScans: (now: Date) =>
      ids(sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'failed', failure = 'scan_timed_out', scanned_at = ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz, ended_at = ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz
               where j.status = 'scanning'
                 and (j.uploaded_at <= ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz - make_interval(mins => ${IMPORT_RULES.scanMinutes}::int)
                      or j.created_at <= ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz - make_interval(hours => ${IMPORT_RULES.archiveHours}::int))
               returning j.id`),

    /** 4.8: a preview not confirmed 24 hours after the scan ended expires, its scan cut down. The ids, whose work folder goes. */
    expirePreviews: (now: Date) =>
      ids(sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'expired', ended_at = ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz, scan = ${CUT_SCAN}
               where j.status = 'ready' and j.scanned_at <= ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz - make_interval(hours => ${IMPORT_RULES.previewHours}::int)
               returning j.id`),

    /**
     * 4.8: an import that has not finished 72 hours after its scan ended stops (time_ran_out), its seed cleared;
     * published posts stay. The ids, whose work folder goes.
     */
    stopTimedOut: (now: Date) =>
      ids(sql`update import_jobs j set status = 'stopped', stop_reason = 'time_ran_out', seed = null, ended_at = ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz
               where j.status in ('preparing', 'publishing') and j.scanned_at <= ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz - make_interval(hours => ${IMPORT_RULES.workHours}::int)
               returning j.id`),

    /**
     * 7.5 step 7: the picks of every import that has ended, and the rows of imports that ended more than 30 days ago and
     * that no post names (a post's import_job_id holds its row, 6.1; the purge clears a deleted post's). A row in an
     * active state or undoing is never one of them, so import_jobs_delete has nothing to refuse.
     */
    async retention(now: Date): Promise<{ picks: number; rows: number }> {
      const picks = await rows<{ ref: number }>(
        db,
        sql`delete from import_picks p using import_jobs j where j.id = p.import_job_id and j.status in ${ENDED} returning p.ref`,
      );
      const gone = await rows<{ id: string }>(
        db,
        sql`delete from import_jobs j
             where j.status in ('done', 'stopped', 'undone', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'expired')
               and j.ended_at <= ${now.toISOString()}::timestamptz - make_interval(days => ${IMPORT_RULES.recordDays}::int)
               and not exists (select 1 from posts p where p.import_job_id = j.id)
            returning j.id`,
      );
      return { picks: picks.length, rows: gone.length };
    },

    /** The state of each of these imports that has a row (7.5 step 8 judges files by it). */
    async statuses(of: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, ImportStatus>> {
      if (of.length === 0) return new Map();
      const found = await rows<{ id: string; status: ImportStatus }>(
        db,
        sql`select j.id, j.status::text as status from import_jobs j where j.id = any(string_to_array(${of.join(",")}, ',')::uuid[])`,
      );
      return new Map(found.map((row) => [row.id, row.status]));
    },

    /**
     * A pick (4.4) written or changed: the first write takes the line's facts with it (migration 0046), a later one changes
     * only whether the line is left out and its descriptions. import_picks_guard refuses it unless the import is ready,
     * which the caller answers wrong_state.
     */
    async upsertPick(jobId: string, pick: PickRow): Promise<void> {
      await db.execute(sql`
        insert into import_picks (import_job_id, ref, left_out, alts, month, marks, described)
        values (${jobId}::uuid, ${pick.ref}::int, ${pick.leftOut}, ${pick.alts === null ? null : JSON.stringify(pick.alts)}::jsonb, ${pick.month}, ${pick.marks}::smallint, ${pick.described}::smallint)
        on conflict (import_job_id, ref) do update set left_out = excluded.left_out, alts = excluded.alts`);
    },

    /** The picks of an import, all of them or those of these lines. */
```
