### Replace `infra/caddy/Caddyfile` (whole file)

```text
{
  auto_https off
  admin off
}

# Caddy's own 404 for an API path a site does not serve, in the API's error envelope, so the page's parser reads it as it
# reads the API's own 404. Nothing behind it is asked.
(api_not_found) {
  header -Server
  header Content-Type application/json
  header Cache-Control no-store
  respond `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"No such route"}}` 404
}

# The page's security headers (3a; 3f, section 7.12): one block for the app's files and for a post's page, so every answer
# of the page carries the same ones, whatever status the post's page gets.
(app_page_headers) {
  header {
    Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
    X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
    X-Frame-Options "DENY"
    Referrer-Policy "no-referrer"
    Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()"
    # challenges.cloudflare.com serves the Turnstile widget script and its iframe (sign-in screens).
    Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://challenges.cloudflare.com; frame-src https://challenges.cloudflare.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'"
    -Server
  }
}

# The app's shell, the same bytes for every post's page: the page itself decides what to show.
(app_shell) {
  root * /srv
  rewrite * /index.html
}

# The app's site while it is open (APP_SITE=open, the default).
(app_site_open) {
  # A client from the push network (ntfy and the watcher, 3f) is refused here: until the push site, only cloudflared could
  # reach Caddy. The handles below that reach anything each answer it 403 first: a handle of this matcher alone would be
  # sorted after the path handles. PUSH_SUBNET is the network's fixed subnet, from Compose.
  @push remote_ip {$PUSH_SUBNET}

  # The staff API belongs to the console's site below, on an origin of its own: the app's site never forwards it. Each of
  # these handles matches one path, longer than /api/*, and Caddy puts such handles most specific first, so they come
  # ahead of the API proxy below wherever they are written.
  handle /api/staff {
    import api_not_found
  }
  handle /api/staff/* {
    import api_not_found
  }

  # The API. Its own headers pass through untouched: its CSP is the strict one for JSON and images.
  handle /api/* {
    # Image uploads. The API counts bytes itself and stops at 20 MiB; this is the second line behind it.
    @upload path /api/media
    request_body @upload {
      max_size 25MB
    }
    # 3b (design, section 7.3): a chunk of an import's archive, 8 MiB at most, which the API counts itself too. 9MB, in
    # decimal megabytes, is the chunk and some slack (IMPORT_RULES.chunkBodyBytes).
    @import_chunk {
      method PUT
      path_regexp ^/api/imports/[0-9a-f-]{36}/archive$
    }
    request_body @import_chunk {
      max_size 9MB
    }
    # Everything else is JSON, and small. The API caps it at 64 KiB too.
    @json {
      not path /api/media
      not {
        method PUT
        path_regexp ^/api/imports/[0-9a-f-]{36}/archive$
      }
    }
    request_body @json {
      max_size 64KB
    }
    header -Server
    respond @push 403
    reverse_proxy api:3000 {
      # Behind the tunnel cloudflared sets CF-Connecting-IP and the API needs it; anywhere else a
      # client could set it, so Caddy drops it. Decided at build time by the TUNNEL argument.
      import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy
    }
  }

  # A post's page (3f design, sections 5 and 7.12): the app's shell under the status the API gives the post, so that a
  # check from outside reads 404 for a post that is not public and never 451. Caddy asks GET /api/posts/<id>/status, with
  # the visitor's address and cookies as every proxied request carries them (the route reads no session, and the
  # global limit counts the question against the visitor): 204 gives the shell with 200, 404 the same shell with 404,
  # and any other answer (a 429 of the global limit) the shell with 200, as before; handle_errors below does the same
  # when the API cannot be asked. Only the status line differs: the bytes and the headers are the same in every case,
  # which Task 4's first step checked on this image (Caddy 2.11.4).
  handle /post/* {
    respond @push 403
    import app_page_headers
    header Cache-Control "no-cache"
    encode gzip
    reverse_proxy api:3000 {
      import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy
      method GET
      rewrite /api/posts/{http.request.uri.path.1}/status
      @shown status 204
      handle_response @shown {
        import app_shell
        file_server
      }
      @gone status 404
      handle_response @gone {
        import app_shell
        file_server {
          status 404
        }
      }
      handle_response {
        import app_shell
        file_server
      }
    }
  }

  # The web app: static files, the page's security headers, and caching by kind of file.
  handle {
    respond @push 403
    root * /srv
    encode gzip
    import app_page_headers
    # The page is revalidated on every load, so a deploy is seen at once; the hashed bundles never change.
    @immutable path /_expo/* /assets/*
    header @immutable Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
    @page {
      not path /_expo/* /assets/*
    }
    header @page Cache-Control "no-cache"
    try_files {path} /index.html
    file_server
  }

  # A post's page when the API cannot be asked (stopped, or not answering): the shell with 200, as before the status.
  # Every other error is answered as Caddy answers it without this block.
  handle_errors {
    @postpage path /post/*
    handle @postpage {
      import app_page_headers
      header Cache-Control "no-cache"
      encode gzip
      import app_shell
      file_server {
        status 200
      }
    }
  }
}

# The app's site while it is closed (APP_SITE=closed; 3f design, section 7.17, a restore): 503 with one fixed sentence to
# every path, the API's included, and nothing else asked or served. The console's site is unchanged.
(app_site_closed) {
  handle {
    header -Server
    header Content-Type "text/plain; charset=utf-8"
    header Cache-Control "no-store"
    respond "korbat is closed for maintenance. Please come back later." 503
  }
}

# The app's site. APP_SITE (open, the default, or closed) is read when Caddy starts and names the snippet that is the
# site: any other value names no snippet, and Caddy refuses to start rather than leave the site open during a restore.
:8080 {
  import app_site_{$APP_SITE:open}
}

# The staff console (3a design, section 8): a site of its own for the console's own origin, CONSOLE_ORIGIN. It serves the
# console's page and proxies the staff API and nothing else. It is always built and always serves the page; the API alone
# switches the console on, and while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset every staff path answers 404, which the page explains. Its
# handles each match two paths or none, so Caddy keeps them in the order written: the staff API, the rest of the API, the
# console's files.
:8090 {
  # A client from the push network (3f) is refused, as on the app's site. This handle's matcher names no path, like the
  # two below, so Caddy keeps it first, as written.
  @push remote_ip {$PUSH_SUBNET}
  handle @push {
    header -Server
    respond 403
  }

  # The staff API, proxied as the app's site proxies /api/*. No header_up Host: the API's staff gate compares the Host the
  # browser sent with CONSOLE_ORIGIN. Caddy still replaces whatever X-Forwarded-* headers a client sent with its own.
  @staff path /api/staff /api/staff/*
  handle @staff {
    # Staff requests are small JSON. The API caps them at 64 KiB too.
    request_body {
      max_size 64KB
    }
    header -Server
    reverse_proxy api:3000 {
      # As on the app's site: the per-IP sign-in limits key on CF-Connecting-IP, which only cloudflared may set.
      import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy
    }
  }

  # The rest of the API is the app's, never the console's.
  @api path /api /api/*
  handle @api {
    import api_not_found
  }

  # The console's page, from /console, a folder outside the app's /srv, so the app's site can never serve it. Its policy
  # is the strict one of section 3: everything from this origin only, no inline script or style, and Trusted Types with no
  # policy, so no HTML or script sink can be used. apps/admin/site-headers.mjs holds the same headers for the development
  # server, and apps/admin/test/console-site.test.ts keeps the two equal.
  handle {
    root * /console
    encode gzip
    header {
      Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types 'none'"
      Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
      X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
      X-Frame-Options "DENY"
      Referrer-Policy "no-referrer"
      Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin"
      Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy "same-origin"
      # WebAuthn for the console itself only; no camera, microphone or position for anyone.
      Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), publickey-credentials-get=(self), publickey-credentials-create=(self)"
      -Server
    }
    # The hashed script and stylesheet never change under their names. Everything else, the page above all, is neither
    # stored nor transformed: no-transform stops Cloudflare injecting scripts the policy would block on every page view.
    # `file` holds only when the path names a file of the build, so the page answered for a missing /assets/ name (the
    # fallback below) is never kept for a year under that name.
    @immutable {
      path /assets/*
      file
    }
    header @immutable Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
    @page {
      not {
        path /assets/*
        file
      }
    }
    header @page Cache-Control "no-store, no-transform"
    try_files {path} /index.html
    file_server
  }
}

# The phones' push site (3f design, section 5), for the push hostname (API_PUSH_ORIGIN): only the two topics'
# subscriptions reach ntfy, by GET, which is what the ntfy app sends: the stream a phone holds open (ws, json, sse; both
# topics joined by a comma in one request, in either order), with its replay of what it missed (since=), and the check of
# a user's access (auth). Everything else is Caddy's own 404, ntfy's account API, /v1/config and /v1/stats among them:
# they answer any caller otherwise. Publishing is the watcher's alone, on the push network.
:8091 {
  @subscribe {
    method GET
    path_regexp ^/(korbat-oncall|korbat-all)(,(korbat-oncall|korbat-all))?/(ws|json|sse|auth)$
  }
  handle @subscribe {
    header -Server
    reverse_proxy ntfy:2586 {
      # As on the other sites: a client-set CF-Connecting-IP is dropped unless TUNNEL=on. ntfy reads the client from
      # X-Forwarded-For (behind-proxy); behind the tunnel that header takes CF-Connecting-IP's value (the Dockerfile).
      import /etc/caddy/cf-header.caddy
      import /etc/caddy/push-header.caddy
    }
  }
  handle {
    header -Server
    respond 404
  }
}
```

### Replace `infra/compose.yml` (whole file)

```yaml
name: korbat

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options: { max-size: "20m", max-file: "5" }

x-node-common: &node-common
  restart: unless-stopped
  read_only: true
  tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  logging: *logging

services:
  postgres:
    # PostgreSQL 18. From 18 on the image keeps the cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/<major>/docker, so
    # the volume is mounted one level up and a later major can pg_upgrade inside it. A cluster from the
    # earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) is moved over by scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs.
    image: postgres:18.6-alpine@sha256:77f585114c32fbca283dc835b0596f4e52b51b4c6662d7810b2f4084f60a1873
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 1g
    memswap_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}
      # The contact point's watcher's role (3f), which 01-roles.sh makes on a new data directory. Not required: a stack
      # without the watcher runs without it.
      KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}
    volumes:
      - pgdata18:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ./postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    # watch: the watcher's own network to the database, which holds nothing else.
    networks: [data, watch]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    # Valkey, the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, under the service name the URLs already use. A password
    # is required: nothing on the data network may read the session cache without it.
    image: valkey/valkey:9.1.2-alpine@sha256:48332870af354a799964c0012ae1194a0bf2bf894eb508f945810596dc2d8d11
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 384m
    memswap_limit: 384m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set REDIS_PASSWORD in infra/.env}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "exec valkey-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --requirepass $$REDIS_PASSWORD"]
    volumes:
    # A fresh volume: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into `redisdata`, and that
    # volume held only transient state (limits, codes in flight, cached sessions, queued image jobs).
      - valkeydata:/data
    networks: [data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "VALKEYCLI_AUTH=$$REDIS_PASSWORD valkey-cli ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  counts:
    # 3d review H3: the recipients' count alone (the day's salt and the month's and the days' sketches), in a Valkey of
    # its own that writes nothing to disk: no append-only file, no snapshot, no volume. The redis service keeps an
    # append-only file of every write, which would hold the salt and each value added to a sketch long after 26 hours.
    # A restart of this service loses the running month's count, which then reads as not recorded (README, The yearly
    # edition). The redis service's pinned image, its password, and the data network alone; no port.
    image: valkey/valkey:9.1.2-alpine@sha256:48332870af354a799964c0012ae1194a0bf2bf894eb508f945810596dc2d8d11
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 96m
    memswap_limit: 96m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set REDIS_PASSWORD in infra/.env}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "exec valkey-server --appendonly no --save '' --maxmemory 48mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --requirepass $$REDIS_PASSWORD"]
    networks: [data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "VALKEYCLI_AUTH=$$REDIS_PASSWORD valkey-cli ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    <<: *node-common
    restart: "no"
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
    command: ["node", "dist/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: postgres://korbat_migrate:${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      MIGRATIONS_DIR: /app/migrations
      # `staff.js enroll` runs here, as the migrator, the one role the running API never holds, and records on each link
      # the console's origin and relying party ID it is issued for. Empty, the console is off and enroll refuses.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # 3f: staff.js order-open runs here too, and reads the home state (whether an order is cross-border) and the app's
      # origin (how a link is read, as the console's route reads it). Neither is required: enroll and the migrations run
      # without them, and order-open refuses with one sentence while either is empty.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:-}
    networks: [data]
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }

  api:
    <<: *node-common
    # The image's name, the one Compose gives it by default, written out: notify (3f) runs the same image, so it is
    # built once.
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
      args:
        KORBAT_VERSION: ${KORBAT_VERSION:-0.0.0}
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      # development or production, from infra/.env; production turns on the guards against test keys, plain-http
      # origins and a relay without TLS. The worker below always runs as production.
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
      PORT: "3000"
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_API: postgres://korbat_api:${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      DATABASE_URL_AUTH: postgres://korbat_auth:${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379
      # 3d review H3: the recipients' count, in the counts service, which writes nothing to disk.
      COUNTS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@counts:6379
      TRUSTED_ORIGINS: ${API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-}
      # Which header names the client: the stack refuses to start without a choice.
      TRUST_PROXY: ${API_TRUST_PROXY:?set API_TRUST_PROXY in infra/.env}
      # Auth settings. The stack refuses to start while any of these is missing from infra/.env.
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:?set API_APP_ORIGIN in infra/.env}
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: ${API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY:?set API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY in infra/.env}
      IP_HASH_KEY: ${API_IP_HASH_KEY:?set API_IP_HASH_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEY: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEY:?set API_TOTP_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      # Encrypts a signed-out notifier's name and address; earlier keys stay accepted for decryption.
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY:?set API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY:?set API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in infra/.env}
      SMTP_URL: ${API_SMTP_URL:?set API_SMTP_URL in infra/.env}
      MAIL_FROM: ${API_MAIL_FROM:?set API_MAIL_FROM in infra/.env}
      TERMS_VERSION: ${API_TERMS_VERSION:?set API_TERMS_VERSION in infra/.env}
      # The verified badge's phone check. off (the default) hides the badge; vonage needs the two credentials.
      VERIFY_PROVIDER: ${API_VERIFY_PROVIDER:-off}
      VONAGE_API_KEY: ${API_VONAGE_API_KEY:-}
      VONAGE_API_SECRET: ${API_VONAGE_API_SECRET:-}
      VERIFY_BRAND: ${API_VERIFY_BRAND:-korbat}
      # Passkeys. Empty values leave the API's defaults: the host of APP_ORIGIN as the RP ID and korbat as the name.
      WEBAUTHN_RP_ID: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID:-}
      WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME:-}
      # The staff console, served by Caddy's second site: the origin staff open it at, and the RP ID staff keys are bound
      # to (empty means the console's hostname). An empty origin switches the console off: every /api/staff path then
      # answers 404. The migrate service gets the same two values for `staff.js enroll`.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # Moderation: the UTC hour of the daily release of decisions to those who reported, the queue's emergency switch, and
      # the retention job's switch, which is off only for a restore window (README, Restoring, step 5).
      MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: ${API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR:-7}
      MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN: ${API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN:-off}
      MODERATION_RETENTION: ${API_MODERATION_RETENTION:-on}
      # Authorities' orders (3f): whether the alert tick judges the alert channel's health. Empty means on in production;
      # off until the contact point's mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
      NOTIFY: ${API_NOTIFY:-}
      # The operator's Member State, a state whose facts the contracts hold (DE is filled in), and the published contact
      # point for authorities. Both empty until the owner's list is done; the home state is required once the contact
      # point is set.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      CONTACT_POINT: ${API_CONTACT_POINT:-}
      # 3f Task 5: whether a deletion keeps an account's address, at most seven days, while a report of its sealed images
      # to the authorities is owed. Empty means on; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once.
      REPORT_HOLD: ${API_REPORT_HOLD:-}
      # 3d: the app's site switch, Caddy's (3f), handed to the API too, which refuses a test adapter while the site is open.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
      # 3d Task 3: the purge of an image's copies at the edge once it stops being public: off (empty, the default), test
      # (refused while APP_SITE is open) or cloudflare, which needs the zone's id, the API token with the one permission
      # Zone, Cache Purge, and the public hostname images are served under (README, The edge).
      EDGE_PURGE: ${API_EDGE_PURGE:-}
      EDGE_ZONE_ID: ${API_EDGE_ZONE_ID:-}
      EDGE_API_TOKEN: ${API_EDGE_API_TOKEN:-}
      EDGE_HOST: ${API_EDGE_HOST:-}
      # 3d Task 4: whether readers without an account are counted among the recipients, each day's by a keyed digest of
      # the network and the browser's name under a salt that lives 26 hours; on unless set to off (README, The yearly edition).
      RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: ${API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT:-}
      # 3d Task 5: the audit head's daily value. Its outside timestamp: off (empty, the default), test (refused while
      # APP_SITE is open) or rfc3161, which needs the timestamp authority's https address; and the one address the
      # keeper's daily mail goes to, empty for none (README, The yearly edition).
      HEAD_WITNESS: ${API_HEAD_WITNESS:-}
      HEAD_WITNESS_URL: ${API_HEAD_WITNESS_URL:-}
      HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL: ${API_HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL:-}
      # 3d Task 6: the R1 check, which the worker reads too (unprefixed): off (empty, the default), test (refused while
      # APP_SITE is open) or onnx, not in this build; whether a score over the threshold withholds its image (off unless
      # on); and the two days of the owner's impact assessment, empty for none.
      R1_CLASSIFIER: ${R1_CLASSIFIER:-}
      AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS:-}
      # 3d Task 7: the comparison of uploads with known material (unprefixed, as the design names it beside R1_CLASSIFIER):
      # off (empty, the default), test (refused while APP_SITE is open) or a source's name, which no adapter of this build
      # answers; whether an acting match on a post seals its images (on unless off); and its two days, empty for none. The
      # worker is not handed it: it computes no perceptual hash in this build.
      MEDIA_MATCH: ${MEDIA_MATCH:-}
      AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH:-}
      AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH_ACTS: ${API_AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH_ACTS:-}
      # Images. The API writes uploads and only reads what the worker stored.
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES: ${MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES:-2147483648}
      MEDIA_RECONCILE: ${MEDIA_RECONCILE:-on}
      # 3b: import from other platforms (README, Importing posts). Imports on unless off; images off unless on, which the
      # API refuses while MEDIA_MATCH is off; the sources a new import may name (bluesky only by the owner's choice); the
      # uploads and scans on the site at once; the imported images an hour (at most 600); the free space kept on
      # import-archives beyond an archive and its scan. The API writes the archives and only reads the importer's output.
      IMPORTS: ${API_IMPORTS:-on}
      IMPORT_IMAGES: ${API_IMPORT_IMAGES:-off}
      IMPORT_SOURCES: ${API_IMPORT_SOURCES:-x,mastodon}
      IMPORT_MAX_ACTIVE: ${API_IMPORT_MAX_ACTIVE:-2}
      IMPORT_IMAGES_PER_HOUR: ${API_IMPORT_IMAGES_PER_HOUR:-600}
      IMPORT_MIN_FREE_BYTES: ${API_IMPORT_MIN_FREE_BYTES:-2147483648}
      IMPORT_ARCHIVES_DIR: /import/archives
      IMPORT_WORK_DIR: /import/work
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
      - import-archives:/import/archives
      - import-work:/import/work:ro
    networks: [app, data]
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      redis: { condition: service_healthy }
      counts: { condition: service_healthy }
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # The image worker runs the decoder, the most exploitable code in the stack. It has no network at
  # all, no credentials and no capabilities: it reads uploads and writes the store, and that is
  # everything it can reach. The memory limit was sized on worst-case images (2b design, Research).
  worker:
    <<: *node-common
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/worker/Dockerfile
    network_mode: none
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 768m
    memswap_limit: 768m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 64
    tmpfs: ["/tmp:size=64m"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      # 3d Task 6: the R1 check's scorer, the API's setting (off when empty), and the site's switch, which the worker reads
      # only to refuse a test scorer while the site is open.
      R1_CLASSIFIER: ${R1_CLASSIFIER:-}
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads:ro
      - media-store:/media/store
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/media/store/heartbeat', 'utf8')).at < 60000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4

  # The importer (3b design, section 7.1; decision 1) parses the archives people upload, hostile input in three formats.
  # Like the worker it has no network, no capabilities and no credentials: no database, no Valkey, no secret but the
  # account key each job brings. It reads import-archives and writes import-work, and that is everything it can reach.
  importer:
    <<: *node-common
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/importer/Dockerfile
    network_mode: none
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    cpus: 0.5
    pids_limit: 32
    tmpfs: ["/tmp:size=16m"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      IMPORT_ARCHIVES_DIR: /import/archives
      IMPORT_WORK_DIR: /import/work
    volumes:
      - import-archives:/import/archives:ro
      - import-work:/import/work
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/import/work/heartbeat', 'utf8')).at < 60000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4

  # The contact point's watcher (3f design, section 5): the API's image with dist/notify.js, under the profile notify. It
  # reads the contact-point mailbox over IMAP and publishes the alerts to ntfy. On the network watch it reaches PostgreSQL
  # as korbat_notify, whose grants are four tables, and nothing else; on push it reaches ntfy. It never joins data, where
  # the API listens and the limit store is. It exits rather than hang, and Docker starts it again. No setting of it is
  # required by Compose: the program names the one it is missing and exits.
  notify:
    <<: *node-common
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["node", "dist/notify.js"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    # Measured in this image (3f Task 1): about 82 MB resident idle, a peak of 93 MB during a first read of 10,000 old
    # messages, which took 21 seconds and fell back to 81 MB; under this limit the container's peak was 85 MB, with no
    # kill. 128 MB keeps more than a third above that peak.
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:-production}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_NOTIFY: postgres://korbat_notify:${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_USER: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_USER:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK:-}
      NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN:-}
    # A fixed address on push (3f's review, operations3), which infra/ntfy/server.yml exempts from ntfy's request limit
    # (visitor-request-limit-exempt-hosts): ntfy lets any one address publish 60 times and then once every 5 seconds (lab
    # L1), which would hold an order's alert behind a flood of contact mail. It lies inside PUSH_SUBNET, at the top of
    # the range, which Docker hands out last; change it, and the file's line, with the subnet.
    networks:
      watch: {}
      push:
        ipv4_address: ${NOTIFY_PUSH_IP:-172.16.91.254}
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      ntfy: { condition: service_started }
    # The watcher writes the time of every round it ends; two minutes without one is a hang.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - Number(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/korbat-notify-beat', 'utf8')) < 120000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # The hand-over of one seal's files (3f design, sections 5 and 7.14), under the profile handover, started by the operator
  # alone: docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests. The API's
  # image with dist/handover.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no credential, no capability,
  # the image store and (3d) the quarantine read-only, the quarantine looked in first. It has no bind mount here: the
  # directory for the archive is an argument of the command (an empty source would stop every Compose command of the
  # stack), on an encrypted volume owned by uid 1000, the image's user node, the only place it can write. No setting of
  # it is required.
  handover:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["handover"]
    command: ["node", "dist/handover.js"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro

  # The quarantine's mover (3d design, sections 5 and 7.1), under the profile quarantine, started by the operator alone:
  # docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt, with the list that
  # staff.js quarantine-list printed, and the receipt then recorded by staff.js quarantine-record (the README,
  # Quarantine). The API's image with dist/quarantine.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no
  # environment, no credential, no capability and a read-only root; the image store and the quarantine read-write, and
  # nothing else. Its two roots are arguments of its entry point, and it refuses to start without both; what follows the
  # service's name on the command line (--lost, --inventory) is appended to them. It is the one service that writes the
  # quarantine; handover reads it, and the api, migrate and worker services never mount it.
  quarantine:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["quarantine"]
    entrypoint: ["node", "dist/quarantine.js", "/media/store", "/media/quarantine"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine

  # The push server (3f design, section 5), under the profile notify, never linked into korbat's programs: ntfy at its
  # pinned release, reading its users, rights and tokens from infra/ntfy/server.yml (git-ignored, made from
  # server.yml.example), mounted read-only, since Compose would blank the $2a$10$ of a password hash in a variable. Only
  # on push, which is internal: it has no route out, so nothing is forwarded upstream. Its cache and auth files are on its
  # volume, at /var/tmp, the one directory of the image its user may write to.
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.28.0@sha256:6ef4b819f722fccdc036af611c4774cfdc2de821ab74fdd48bbf4c9d6f8973da
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["serve", "--config", "/etc/ntfy/server.yml"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    user: "1000:1000"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy-data:/var/tmp
    networks: [push]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:2586/v1/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 4

  # Caddy serves the web app on port 8080, proxying /api, the staff console on port 8090, proxying only /api/staff, and
  # (3f) the phones' push site on port 8091, proxying only the two topics' subscriptions to ntfy. It runs as its own
  # user, sees only the API and ntfy, and is the only thing cloudflared can reach. A client from the push network (ntfy,
  # the watcher) is refused 403 on the app's and the console's sites.
  caddy:
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/caddy/Dockerfile
      args:
        EXPO_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY:?set WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in infra/.env}
        KORBAT_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
        TUNNEL: ${TUNNEL:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE: ${WEB_BADGE:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL:?set WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL in infra/.env}
        # 3f: the terms' contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State; neither is required (Before going public).
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT: ${WEB_CONTACT_POINT:-}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE: ${WEB_HOME_STATE:-}
    depends_on:
      api: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      # The push network's subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse (3f).
      PUSH_SUBNET: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}
      # The app's site, open (the default) or closed: closed answers 503 to every path while a restore is checked (3f,
      # section 7.17). Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    networks: [edge, app, push]

  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.1@sha256:b269e8abd07a5bf6f3f4be65d5050b2174eca89c56a0241a8ff32a16aec454e4
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    profiles: ["tunnel"]
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run"]
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}
    networks: [edge]
    depends_on:
      - caddy

# cloudflared reaches only Caddy, Caddy reaches only the API and ntfy, and the API alone reaches the data services, but
# for the watcher's own network to PostgreSQL (3f).
networks:
  edge:
  app:
  data:
  # The watcher and PostgreSQL, nothing else. Not internal: the mail host's port 993 is reached through its gateway.
  watch:
  # ntfy, the watcher and Caddy. Internal: no route out. Its fixed subnet is what the app's and the console's sites refuse.
  push:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}

volumes:
  # PostgreSQL 18. The earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) stays until scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs has
  # moved it and you remove it by hand.
  pgdata18:
  valkeydata:
  # Uploads wait here for the worker and are deleted once processed. Nothing in it needs a backup.
  media-uploads:
  # The images korbat serves. Back it up together with the database.
  media-store:
  # 3b: archives waiting for the importer, deleted when read and within 24 hours. In no backup, by decision: an archive
  # holds the person's messages and other people's data.
  import-archives:
  # 3b: the importer's output, deleted within 72 hours. In no backup.
  import-work:
  # 3d: the files of images sealed for good, moved out of the store by the quarantine service, on the host's encrypted
  # disk. It is in no backup, by decision: a restore never brings a destroyed file back. Owned by uid 1000, mode 0700, the
  # path the API's image makes (the README, Quarantine and Backups).
  media-quarantine:
  # Caddy's state, owned by its own user; the earlier root-owned caddydata and caddyconfig volumes can go.
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  # ntfy's message cache and its auth database (3f). The cache is how a phone gets an alert published while its
  # connection was down; the auth database is rebuilt from infra/ntfy/server.yml at every start.
  ntfy-data:
```

### Replace `packages/contracts/src/imports.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { AltText, MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST } from "./media";
import { FORBIDDEN_CONTROL, FORBIDDEN_FORMAT, normalizePostBody, postLength, visibleLength } from "./text";

/**
 * Import from other platforms (3b design, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-import-3b-design.md, sections 5.1 and 9.3;
 * Task 1): the line the importer writes and the API reads back as hostile input, the importer's summary, the intake's
 * numbers, the person's choice, the views, the closed lists and every number of the design. It imports only zod,
 * ./media and ./text, so social.ts, moderation.ts, staff.ts and account.ts can read ImportSource while they load.
 */

const rules = {
  /** 7.3: a chunk is exactly this long but the last; under Cloudflare's 100 MB and inside its 125-second read timeout. */
  chunkBytes: 8_388_608,
  /** 7.3: the largest archive, 256 chunks; the CHECK of import_jobs.declared_bytes (6.1). */
  maxBytes: 2_147_483_648,
  /** 7.3: Caddy's body limit for a chunk, its "9MB", which Caddy reads as decimal megabytes. */
  chunkBodyBytes: 9_000_000,
  /** 9.4: the app sends a chunk whose hash differed again at most this often. */
  chunkRetries: 3,
  /** 4.2 step 3, decision 21: an account imports once it is this old (import_too_soon). */
  minAccountAgeDays: 7,
  /** Decision 21: an account younger than this publishes at most newAccountMaxPosts posts per import. */
  newAccountDays: 30,
  newAccountMaxPosts: 1_000,
  /** 7.6: the limits. Published imports per account in seven days, imports created per address in a day, and per hour per account. */
  importsPerWeek: 3,
  importsPerAddressDay: 5,
  chunksPerHour: 600,
  actsPerHour: 20,
  picksPerHour: 3_000,
  /** 7.7: the default of IMPORT_MAX_ACTIVE, imports in uploading or scanning on the site at once. */
  maxActiveDefault: 2,
  /** 7.4, 7.7: IMPORT_IMAGES_PER_HOUR's default, and the most it may be set to (it may only be lowered). */
  imagesPerHourDefault: 600,
  imagesPerHourMax: 600,
  /** 7.7: the default of IMPORT_MIN_FREE_BYTES, kept free on import-archives beyond a new import's size and scanWriteBytes. */
  minFreeBytesDefault: 2_147_483_648,
  /** 4.2 step 3, 7.2: the most a scan may write to import-work. */
  scanWriteBytes: 4_294_967_296,
  /** 7.1: the importer rewrites its heartbeat this often; the API takes no new import once it is older than the second. */
  heartbeatMs: 10_000,
  heartbeatStaleMs: 60_000,
  /** 4.8, decision 4: an archive lives at most this long after its import was created (an upload not complete then expires, a scan not done fails). */
  archiveHours: 24,
  /** 4.8: a scan not done this long after the upload ended fails (scan_timed_out). */
  scanMinutes: 45,
  /** 4.8: a preview not confirmed this long after the scan ended expires. */
  previewHours: 24,
  /** 4.8, decision 19: an imported image whose check is not answered this long after its upload is left out. */
  checkHours: 24,
  /** 4.8: an import not finished this long after its scan ended is stopped; the work folder never outlives it (the terms' three days). */
  workHours: 72,
  /** 4.8, decision 25: a finished import's record stays at least this long after its end. */
  recordDays: 30,
  /** 5.3 step 7, decision 13: a longer text is skipped (too_long_to_read). */
  textMax: 30_000,
  /** Decision 13: a post over this many code points is long; shortened, it is cut to this many with its ellipsis. */
  shortenTo: 1_000,
  /** 5.4: items read, posts kept and images kept by one scan. */
  maxItems: 1_000_000,
  maxPosts: 50_000,
  maxImages: 5_000,
  /** 5.4: a date before the first tweet, or more than futureDays after the import was created, is skipped (date_out_of_range). */
  earliestDate: "2006-03-21",
  futureDays: 1,
  /** 5.5, 5.6: one JSON element of a data file, in bytes and levels (item_too_large). */
  itemMaxBytes: 1_048_576,
  itemMaxDepth: 64,
  /** 5.5: X's data/manifest.js, and the highest N of data/tweets-part<N>.js. */
  manifestMaxBytes: 1_048_576,
  tweetsPartsMax: 99,
  /** 5.7: a CAR's blocks, and its MST's levels and entries a node. */
  carBlockMaxBytes: 1_000_000,
  carMaxBlocks: 2_000_000,
  mstMaxDepth: 48,
  mstMaxEntries: 4_096,
  /** 7.2: the zip reader's limits: entries, central directory, a name, a data file, the ratio, the allowlisted entries' sum. */
  zipMaxEntries: 200_000,
  zipDirectoryMaxBytes: 67_108_864,
  zipNameMaxBytes: 512,
  zipDataMaxBytes: 1_073_741_824,
  zipMaxRatio: 100,
  zipTotalMaxBytes: 4_294_967_296,
  /** 7.1, 7.5: the file protocol's caps: job.json, summary.json, a line of posts.jsonl, and posts.jsonl (whose lines are at most maxPosts). */
  jobFileMaxBytes: 4_096,
  summaryMaxBytes: 65_536,
  lineMaxBytes: 262_144,
  postsFileMaxBytes: 1_073_741_824,
  /** 7.1: the third start of a scan fails it (interrupted); the watchdog ends a scan; the loop sleeps this long when idle. */
  maxAttempts: 3,
  watchdogMs: 1_800_000,
  idleMs: 1_000,
  /** 6.1: the CHECKs of import_jobs (refused_words in code points, scan and choice in bytes), import_picks.alts, import_keys.key and the seed. */
  refusedWordsMax: 80,
  scanMaxBytes: 262_144,
  choiceMaxBytes: 1_024,
  altsMaxBytes: 16_384,
  keyBytes: 32,
  seedBytes: 32,
  /** 7.4: imported images in processing on the site at once. */
  imagesInFlight: 2,
  /** 7.5: import-drive's interval and lock, the intake's batch of keys, a batch of posts, batches a round, the orphan pass. */
  driveIntervalMs: 5_000,
  driveLockMs: 60_000,
  keyBatch: 1_000,
  batchPosts: 200,
  publishBatchesPerRound: 10,
  undoBatchesPerRound: 5,
  orphanEveryRounds: 10,
  orphanAgeMs: 3_600_000,
  /** 9.2: lines a page of the preview, pages kept, samples and a sample's bytes, imports listed. */
  pageLines: 50,
  maxPages: 1_000,
  samples: 3,
  sampleMaxBytes: 262_144,
  listMax: 20,
};

/**
 * Every number of the design (section 9.3), as 3d's AUTOMATION_RULES holds its own: the CHECK constants of Task 2's
 * migrations mirror the ones of 6.1, a database test holds them equal, and the terms print their hours and days from
 * here (11.3). Settings that the owner may change are named for their defaults.
 */
export const IMPORT_RULES: Readonly<typeof rules> = rules;

export const IMPORT_SOURCE_KINDS = ["x", "mastodon", "bluesky"] as const;
export const ImportSource = z.enum(IMPORT_SOURCE_KINDS);
export type ImportSource = z.infer<typeof ImportSource>;

/** The twelve states of section 4.1. */
export const ImportStatus = z.enum(["uploading", "scanning", "ready", "preparing", "publishing", "done", "stopped", "undoing", "undone", "failed", "cancelled", "expired"]);
export type ImportStatus = z.infer<typeof ImportStatus>;

/** The active states: an account has at most one import in them (import_jobs_one_active). undoing is not one. */
export const IMPORT_ACTIVE_STATES = ["uploading", "scanning", "ready", "preparing", "publishing"] as const satisfies readonly ImportStatus[];

/** Why a scan failed: import_jobs.failure's CHECK, and a failed summary's member. */
export const IMPORT_FAILURES = [
  "not_this_source",
  "not_an_archive",
  "tar_gz",
  "partial_archive",
  "encrypted",
  "too_many_entries",
  "too_large_uncompressed",
  "bad_entry_name",
  "unreadable",
  "nothing_to_import",
  "scan_timed_out",
  "interrupted",
] as const;
export const ImportFailure = z.enum(IMPORT_FAILURES);
export type ImportFailure = z.infer<typeof ImportFailure>;

/** Why an import was stopped: import_jobs.stop_reason's CHECK. */
export const IMPORT_STOP_REASONS = ["refused_image", "by_author", "by_staff", "time_ran_out"] as const;
export type ImportStopReason = (typeof IMPORT_STOP_REASONS)[number];

/**
 * Why a post is not published. reply, too_long, warning, protected and left_out are counted by the app from the month
 * table and the picks when the choice leaves them out; already_imported and new_account_cap by the intake; the rest by
 * the importer.
 */
export const IMPORT_SKIP_REASONS = [
  "repost",
  "reply",
  "too_long",
  "warning",
  "protected",
  "left_out",
  "not_public",
  "older_version",
  "poll",
  "adult_label",
  "too_long_to_read",
  "date_out_of_range",
  "item_too_large",
  "unreadable",
  "empty",
  "already_imported",
  "over_post_cap",
  "over_item_cap",
  "new_account_cap",
] as const;
export type ImportSkipReason = (typeof IMPORT_SKIP_REASONS)[number];

/** Why an image is not imported. */
export const IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS = ["video", "sensitive", "unsupported", "too_large", "missing_file", "bluesky_no_files", "images_off", "not_chosen", "no_description", "over_image_cap", "failed", "not_checked", "flagged"] as const;
export type ImportImageSkip = (typeof IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS)[number];

/**
 * A line's marks, the facts a choice decides on, as bits: IMPORT_MARKS[i] is the bit 1 << i. reply: its kind is reply;
 * long: its text is over shortenTo code points; warning and protected: the line's members of those names.
 */
export const IMPORT_MARKS = ["reply", "long", "warning", "protected"] as const;

const Count = z.int().min(0);
const Ref = z.int().min(0).max(IMPORT_RULES.maxPosts - 1);
/** A byte offset into posts.jsonl. */
const Offset = z.int().min(0).max(IMPORT_RULES.postsFileMaxBytes);
const Marks = z.int().min(0).max(2 ** IMPORT_MARKS.length - 1);
const Month = z.string().regex(/^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$/);
/** The archive's day, never its second, which with the text would fingerprint the original. */
const Day = z.iso.date();
const Kind = z.enum(["post", "thread", "reply"]);

/**
 * PostText's rule with textMax in place of POST_MAX_LENGTH, and its raw cap scaled the same way (four UTF-16 units a code
 * point). This module's refinements carry no message of their own: no person reads them (the API answers invalid_request
 * and the intake counts a line unreadable), and every byte here is in the app's web bundle.
 */
export const ImportedText = z
  .string()
  .max(IMPORT_RULES.textMax * 4)
  .transform(normalizePostBody)
  .refine((text) => !FORBIDDEN_CONTROL.test(text))
  .refine((text) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(text))
  .refine((text) => postLength(text) <= IMPORT_RULES.textMax);
export type ImportedText = z.infer<typeof ImportedText>;

/**
 * The only names the work folder's media/ may hold: <ref>-<position>.<jpg|png|webp>, the ref without leading zeros and
 * below maxPosts, the position from 0, as refs count, and below MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST (so 0 to 3).
 */
export const ImportMediaFile = z
  .string()
  .regex(/^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,4})-[0-3][.](jpg|png|webp)$/)
  .refine((file) => Number.parseInt(file, 10) < IMPORT_RULES.maxPosts);
export type ImportMediaFile = z.infer<typeof ImportMediaFile>;

/** One kept post, one line of posts.jsonl (5.1). The importer writes it; the API parses every line with this schema. */
export const ImportedPost = z
  .strictObject({
    /** Its line in posts.jsonl, from 0; lines are in ascending order of `at`. */
    ref: Ref,
    /** HMAC-SHA256 of the source and the source post's id under the account's import key, as 64 lowercase hex. */
    key: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/),
    /** The date the archive gives the post, UTC, whole seconds. */
    at: z.iso.datetime({ offset: false, precision: 0 }),
    /** post: the account's own top-level post; thread: a reply to its own post; reply: a reply to someone else. */
    kind: Kind,
    /** The ref of the post a `thread` item answers, always lower than its own ref; null otherwise. */
    parent: z.int().min(0).nullable(),
    /** korbat's plain text: converted, cleaned and normalised (5.3); up to textMax code points. */
    text: ImportedText,
    /** Images in the work folder, in order; `alt` is the source's description, normalised, or null. */
    media: z.array(z.strictObject({ file: ImportMediaFile, alt: AltText.nullable() })).max(MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST),
    /** X only: dated inside a period protected-history.js marks as protected (5.5); left out unless chosen. */
    protected: z.boolean(),
    /** Mastodon only: the text begins with a content warning's line (decision 12); left out unless chosen. */
    warning: z.boolean(),
  })
  .refine((post) => (post.kind === "thread") === (post.parent !== null) && (post.parent === null || post.parent < post.ref), { path: ["parent"] })
  .refine((post) => visibleLength(post.text) >= 1 || post.media.length >= 1, { path: ["text"] })
  .refine(
    (post) => {
      const names = post.media.map(({ file }) => file.split(/[-.]/));
      return names.every(([ref]) => Number(ref) === post.ref) && new Set(names.map(([, position]) => position)).size === names.length;
    },
    { path: ["media"] },
  );
export type ImportedPost = z.infer<typeof ImportedPost>;

/** The counts a scan reports and the intake keeps: counts only, every reason from the closed lists. */
const scanCounts = {
  /** Lines written (the summary), or lines the preview offers (the intake: readable, not already imported, not over the new account's cap). */
  posts: Count.max(IMPORT_RULES.maxPosts),
  images: Count.max(IMPORT_RULES.maxImages),
  skipped: z.partialRecord(z.enum(IMPORT_SKIP_REASONS), Count),
  imagesSkipped: z.partialRecord(z.enum(IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS), Count),
  /** Characters removed by 5.3 step 5, and descriptions that became null. */
  cleaned: Count,
  /** Posts that begin with a content warning's line (Mastodon), and links to the source platform replaced by words (5.3 step 3b). */
  warnings: Count,
  sourceLinks: Count,
  /** X posts dated inside a protected period. */
  protectedPosts: Count,
  /** The scan stopped at maxItems (over_item_cap). */
  readInPart: z.boolean(),
};

/** summary.json, the importer's last write for a scan and its commit point (7.1 step 4). The API parses it as hostile input. */
export const ImportSummary = z.discriminatedUnion("status", [
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(1), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("scanned"), ...scanCounts }),
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(1), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("failed"), failure: ImportFailure }),
]);
export type ImportSummary = z.infer<typeof ImportSummary>;

/**
 * A month table: per month, one group per set of marks that occurs, as [marks, posts, images, imagesUndescribed]. In the
 * scan: the lines the preview offers, their images, and those of their images without a source's description. In the
 * picks' counts: [marks, posts left out, images with a source's description in posts left out, images given a
 * description by a pick in posts not left out], so the app's totals stay exact.
 */
const MonthTable = z.array(z.object({ month: Month, groups: z.array(z.tuple([Marks, Count, Count, Count])).max(2 ** IMPORT_MARKS.length) }));

/**
 * What the intake stores in import_jobs.scan (6.1, 7.5 step 2). `fromRef` is the lowest ref that may be published (a
 * new account's newest lines only); `samples` the three newest lines' refs and byte offsets; `pages` every pageLines-th
 * line's byte offset. The move out of ready keeps the counts and fromRef and empties the rest.
 */
export const ImportScanFacts = z.object({
  ...scanCounts,
  months: MonthTable,
  first: Month.nullable(),
  last: Month.nullable(),
  fromRef: Ref,
  samples: z.array(z.object({ ref: Ref, offset: Offset })).max(IMPORT_RULES.samples),
  pages: z.array(Offset).max(IMPORT_RULES.maxPages),
});
export type ImportScanFacts = z.infer<typeof ImportScanFacts>;

/** The person's choice (4.4): a range of months, inclusive, either end open when null; never `from` after `to`. */
export const ImportChoice = z
  .strictObject({
    from: Month.nullable(),
    to: Month.nullable(),
    replies: z.boolean(),
    warnings: z.boolean(),
    protected: z.boolean(),
    images: z.boolean(),
    long: z.enum(["leave", "shorten"]),
  })
  .refine((choice) => choice.from === null || choice.to === null || choice.from <= choice.to, { path: ["to"] });
export type ImportChoice = z.infer<typeof ImportChoice>;

/** One line of the preview's list (9.2), with the person's pick: `alts[i]` is the description written for media[i]. */
export const ImportLineView = z.object({
  ref: Ref,
  at: Day,
  kind: Kind,
  marks: Marks,
  text: z.string(),
  media: z.array(z.object({ file: ImportMediaFile, alt: z.string().nullable() })),
  leftOut: z.boolean(),
  alts: z.array(z.string().nullable()),
});
export type ImportLineView = z.infer<typeof ImportLineView>;

/** A pick (4.4): leave the line out or not, and a description for each image its source gave none, by position in media. */
export const ImportPickRequest = z.strictObject({ leftOut: z.boolean(), alts: z.array(AltText.nullable()).max(MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST) });
export type ImportPickRequest = z.infer<typeof ImportPickRequest>;

/** The pick as saved, and the picks' counts by month and marks. */
export const ImportPickView = z.object({ ref: Ref, leftOut: z.boolean(), alts: z.array(z.string().nullable()), picks: MonthTable });
export type ImportPickView = z.infer<typeof ImportPickView>;

export const CreateImportRequest = z.strictObject({ source: ImportSource, bytes: z.int().min(1).max(IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes) });
export type CreateImportRequest = z.infer<typeof CreateImportRequest>;

/** The statement (decision 14) is part of the request: without it there is nothing to confirm. */
export const ConfirmImportRequest = z.strictObject({ choice: ImportChoice, statement: z.literal(true) });
export type ConfirmImportRequest = z.infer<typeof ConfirmImportRequest>;

/**
 * An import as its owner sees it (9.3). No text but the samples (only in ready) and the refused post's first words, no
 * file name, no source id. `scan` holds the facts without their offsets; `endedByStaff` is the rule's id when an admin
 * ended it; `refusedAt` is the archive's day of the post whose image was refused.
 */
export const ImportView = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  source: ImportSource,
  status: ImportStatus,
  createdAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  endedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  declaredBytes: z.int().min(1).max(IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes),
  receivedBytes: Count.max(IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes),
  chunkBytes: z.int().min(1),
  failure: ImportFailure.nullable(),
  stopReason: z.enum(IMPORT_STOP_REASONS).nullable(),
  endedByStaff: z.string().nullable(),
  scan: ImportScanFacts.omit({ samples: true, pages: true }).nullable(),
  samples: z.array(z.object({ at: Day, text: z.string() })).max(IMPORT_RULES.samples),
  choice: ImportChoice.nullable(),
  picks: MonthTable,
  progress: z.object({ imagesTotal: Count, imagesSettled: Count, postsTotal: Count, postsPublished: Count, postsRemoved: Count, postsLeft: Count }),
  paused: z.boolean(),
  refusalId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  refusedAt: Day.nullable(),
  refusedWords: z.string().nullable(),
  undoable: z.boolean(),
});
export type ImportView = z.infer<typeof ImportView>;

/**
 * Every code the imports endpoints add to ErrorEnvelope.error.code; rate_limited, account_suspended and not_found are shared.
 * import_weekly_limit is the account's three published imports in seven days (import-week), a code of its own so the app
 * says that and not the per-address limit's words, which rate_limited carries (the orchestrator's ruling for Task 4).
 */
export const ImportErrorCode = z.enum([
  "imports_unavailable",
  "import_active",
  "rate_limited",
  "import_weekly_limit",
  "archive_too_large",
  "wrong_state",
  "wrong_offset",
  "chunk_too_large",
  "chunk_mismatch",
  "not_an_archive",
  "statement_required",
  "nothing_chosen",
  "import_too_soon",
  "account_suspended",
  "not_found",
]);
export type ImportErrorCode = z.infer<typeof ImportErrorCode>;
```

### Replace `packages/db/src/schema/imports.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { bigint, boolean, check, date, index, integer, jsonb, pgEnum, pgTable, primaryKey, smallint, text, uniqueIndex, uuid } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { apiRole, bytea, fullAccess, ts } from "./helpers";
import { profiles } from "./identity";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- import from other platforms (3b design, sections 6.1, 6.4 and 6.7; Task 2)
// The three tables of the migration imports. Only the API's imports module names them. The closed lists and numbers are
// the contracts' (packages/contracts/src/imports.ts: IMPORT_SOURCE_KINDS, ImportStatus, IMPORT_ACTIVE_STATES,
// IMPORT_FAILURES, IMPORT_STOP_REASONS and IMPORT_RULES), written out here because this package does not depend on the
// contracts; apps/api/test/integration/import-schema.test.ts holds every migrated CHECK, enum and predicate equal to them.
// The migration's hand-written part adds the triggers that force an insert's columns, walk the states of section 4.1 and
// guard the deletes, and the API role's grants.

/** Where an archive came from. A later source is one more value (section 1.4). */
export const importSource = pgEnum("import_source", ["x", "mastodon", "bluesky"]);

/** The twelve states of section 4.1, in ImportStatus's order. The first five are active. */
export const importStatus = pgEnum("import_status", ["uploading", "scanning", "ready", "preparing", "publishing", "done", "stopped", "undoing", "undone", "failed", "cancelled", "expired"]);

/**
 * One import (6.1): an archive's upload, its scan, the person's choice and the publishing, as one row moving through the
 * twelve states. It holds the source, the state, the times, the choice and counts only: never a file name, a handle or a
 * text, but the first words of a post whose image was refused, shown to the person alone (decision 25). import_jobs_insert
 * forces every column but the id, the owner, the source and the size; import_jobs_guard lets each later column change
 * only by the move that names it. A post names its import (posts.import_job_id), so the row stays while one does.
 */
export const importJobs = pgTable(
  "import_jobs",
  {
    /** Made by the API (randomUUID): it names the import's folders on the two volumes. */
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey(),
    /** No on delete clause: no profile row is ever deleted. */
    ownerId: uuid("owner_id")
      .notNull()
      .references(() => profiles.id),
    source: importSource("source").notNull(),
    /** Forced to uploading at insert. */
    status: importStatus("status").notNull().default("uploading"),
    /** The archive's size as the person's app declared it: 1 byte to IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes. */
    declaredBytes: bigint("declared_bytes", { mode: "number" }).notNull(),
    /** Bytes stored so far; only grows, never past the declared size. */
    receivedBytes: bigint("received_bytes", { mode: "number" }).notNull().default(0),
    /** Forced to clock_timestamp() at insert. */
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    /** Each set once, by the move that names it: into scanning, out of scanning, out of ready by a confirmation. */
    uploadedAt: ts("uploaded_at"),
    scannedAt: ts("scanned_at"),
    confirmedAt: ts("confirmed_at"),
    /** Set by the move into done, stopped, failed, cancelled or expired, and again by the move into undone. */
    endedAt: ts("ended_at"),
    /** IMPORT_FAILURES; set exactly when the state is failed. */
    failure: text("failure"),
    /** IMPORT_STOP_REASONS; set by the move into stopped, and kept through undoing and undone. */
    stopReason: text("stop_reason"),
    /** An admin's end of the whole import (8.7): when, and under which rule. Set together, once. */
    staffEndedAt: ts("staff_ended_at"),
    staffRuleId: text("staff_rule_id"),
    /** The archive's day and first words of the post whose image was refused (8.2). Set together, once. */
    refusedAtOriginal: date("refused_at_original"),
    refusedWords: text("refused_words"),
    /** The intake's numbers (ImportScanFacts); never a text. Set by the move into ready, and cut down by the move out of it. */
    scan: jsonb("scan"),
    /** ImportChoice, the person's statement and the seed come with the confirmation, together and once. */
    choice: jsonb("choice"),
    statedAt: ts("stated_at"),
    /** 32 random bytes from which the import's post and image ids are derived (6.5); cleared when the import ends. */
    seed: bytea("seed"),
    /** Lines of posts.jsonl handled, and images handed to the feeder; each only grows. */
    postCursor: integer("post_cursor").notNull().default(0),
    imageCursor: integer("image_cursor").notNull().default(0),
    /** Progress counts; each only grows. */
    postsPublished: integer("posts_published").notNull().default(0),
    imagesKept: integer("images_kept").notNull().default(0),
    imagesLeftOut: integer("images_left_out").notNull().default(0),
    postsRemoved: integer("posts_removed").notNull().default(0),
    /**
     * 3b Task 4 (the orchestrator's ruling; migration 0046): whether this import brings images, decided once at its
     * creation (IMPORT_IMAGES on, which the API allows only beside a matcher, decision 15) and written into job.json. The
     * API role inserts it and holds no UPDATE of it, so it never changes; the preview's media route reads it from here.
     */
    images: boolean("images").notNull().default(false),
  },
  (t) => [
    // IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes.
    check("import_jobs_declared_bytes", sql`${t.declaredBytes} between 1 and 2147483648`),
    check("import_jobs_received_bytes", sql`${t.receivedBytes} between 0 and ${t.declaredBytes}`),
    // IMPORT_FAILURES.
    check(
      "import_jobs_failure",
      sql`${t.failure} in ('not_this_source', 'not_an_archive', 'tar_gz', 'partial_archive', 'encrypted', 'too_many_entries', 'too_large_uncompressed', 'bad_entry_name', 'unreadable', 'nothing_to_import', 'scan_timed_out', 'interrupted')`,
    ),
    // The state is compared as text, as 3b compares every enum (section 6).
    check("import_jobs_failed", sql`(${t.status}::text = 'failed') = (${t.failure} is not null)`),
    // IMPORT_STOP_REASONS.
    check("import_jobs_stop_reason", sql`${t.stopReason} in ('refused_image', 'by_author', 'by_staff', 'time_ran_out')`),
    // A stopped import has its reason; the reason stays through the undo, and no other state has one.
    check("import_jobs_stopped", sql`(${t.status}::text <> 'stopped' or ${t.stopReason} is not null) and (${t.stopReason} is null or ${t.status}::text in ('stopped', 'undoing', 'undone'))`),
    check("import_jobs_staff", sql`(${t.staffEndedAt} is null) = (${t.staffRuleId} is null)`),
    check("import_jobs_refused", sql`(${t.refusedAtOriginal} is null) = (${t.refusedWords} is null)`),
    // IMPORT_RULES.refusedWordsMax, in code points.
    check("import_jobs_refused_words", sql`char_length(${t.refusedWords}) <= 80`),
    // IMPORT_RULES.scanMaxBytes and choiceMaxBytes, as the bytes of the jsonb's text form.
    check("import_jobs_scan", sql`jsonb_typeof(${t.scan}) = 'object' and octet_length(${t.scan}::text) <= 262144`),
    check("import_jobs_choice", sql`jsonb_typeof(${t.choice}) = 'object' and octet_length(${t.choice}::text) <= 1024`),
    // The statement is never stored without the choice it confirmed, nor the choice without it.
    check("import_jobs_stated", sql`(${t.choice} is null) = (${t.statedAt} is null)`),
    // IMPORT_RULES.seedBytes.
    check("import_jobs_seed", sql`octet_length(${t.seed}) = 32`),
    check(
      "import_jobs_counts",
      sql`${t.postCursor} >= 0 and ${t.imageCursor} >= 0 and ${t.postsPublished} >= 0 and ${t.imagesKept} >= 0 and ${t.imagesLeftOut} >= 0 and ${t.postsRemoved} >= 0`,
    ),
    /**
     * One active import an account (4.1): the five states of IMPORT_ACTIVE_STATES. The enum's labels are literals here, not
     * text: an index predicate takes only immutable expressions, and the cast of an enum to text is not one. The type is
     * created in the same migration, so its labels are usable at once.
     */
    uniqueIndex("import_jobs_one_active").on(t.ownerId).where(sql`status in ('uploading', 'scanning', 'ready', 'preparing', 'publishing')`),
    /** import-drive's rounds, by state and age. */
    index("import_jobs_status_idx").on(t.status, t.createdAt),
    /** The account's list of its imports, and the purge's. */
    index("import_jobs_owner_idx").on(t.ownerId, t.createdAt),
    fullAccess("import_jobs_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * The person's choices post by post (4.4): a line of posts.jsonl left out, and a description for each of its images the
 * source gave none, by position. Written only while the import is ready (import_picks_guard); deleted when the import
 * ends, and with the import's row in any case.
 */
export const importPicks = pgTable(
  "import_picks",
  {
    importJobId: uuid("import_job_id")
      .notNull()
      .references(() => importJobs.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    /** The line's ref, its place in posts.jsonl. */
    ref: integer("ref").notNull(),
    leftOut: boolean("left_out").notNull().default(false),
    /** An array of at most MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST AltText or null, or null. */
    alts: jsonb("alts"),
    /**
     * 3b Task 4 (the orchestrator's ruling; migration 0046): the picked line's month (YYYY-MM), its marks (IMPORT_MARKS as
     * bits) and how many of its images its source described, copied from posts.jsonl when the pick is first written. The
     * picks' counts of ImportView and ImportPickView are summed from these rows alone, so reading an import opens no work
     * file but the samples. The API role inserts them and holds no UPDATE of them: a line's facts never change.
     */
    month: text("month").notNull(),
    marks: smallint("marks").notNull(),
    described: smallint("described").notNull().default(0),
  },
  (t) => [
    primaryKey({ columns: [t.importJobId, t.ref] }),
    check("import_picks_month", sql`${t.month} ~ '^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$'`),
    // IMPORT_MARKS: four bits.
    check("import_picks_marks", sql`${t.marks} between 0 and 15`),
    // MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST.
    check("import_picks_described", sql`${t.described} between 0 and 4`),
    // At most four descriptions (MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST) in IMPORT_RULES.altsMaxBytes, as the bytes of the jsonb's text form:
    // four AltText of 1,000 code points take up to 16,016 (Task 1's amendment). A CASE, so the length is read only of an array.
    check(
      "import_picks_alts",
      sql`case jsonb_typeof(${t.alts}) when 'array' then jsonb_array_length(${t.alts}) <= 4 and octet_length(${t.alts}::text) <= 16384 else ${t.alts} is null end`,
    ),
    fullAccess("import_picks_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
```

### Replace `scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` (whole file)

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Creates or completes the local .env files from their committed examples: infra/.env,
 * apps/api/.env, apps/app/.env, apps/worker/.env and (3b) apps/importer/.env.
 *
 * - `change-me-<word>`          -> 48 random hex characters (passwords)
 * - `change-me-key-<name>`      -> 32 random bytes, base64 (HMAC keys)
 * - `v1:change-me-key-<name>`   -> `v1:` + 32 random bytes, base64 (versioned encryption keys)
 * - `change-me-api|auth|migrate|notify|redis` inside apps/api/.env -> the matching password from infra/.env
 * - Keys used by both the API in Docker (`API_<NAME>` in infra/.env) and the API on the host
 *   (`<NAME>` in apps/api/.env) are generated once and copied to the other file, so both processes
 *   hash, sign and encrypt with the same keys.
 *
 * A value that already exists in a .env file is never changed. Keys that are new in an example
 * are appended. Values are never printed.
 *
 * It also makes infra/ntfy/server.yml (3f) from its committed example when it is missing: the push server's users and
 * tokens, the example's development ones until a real server's are set by hand.
 *
 * It also writes apps/api/.env.test, the environment of the integration tests: apps/api/.env with
 * the database URLs pointing at `<database>_test`, the Redis URL at database 15 and the counts' URL (3d review) at the
 * same Valkey's database 14. That file is
 * derived on every run, so it cannot drift from apps/api/.env. `node scripts/test-db.mjs` creates
 * the database it names.
 *
 * It only serves development: it refuses to run when infra/.env already names a public origin,
 * because production values are set by hand and never generated.
 *
 * Usage: node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs
 */
import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const LINE = /^([A-Z0-9_]+)=(.*)$/;

function parse(text) {
  const map = new Map();
  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const m = LINE.exec(line);
    if (m) map.set(m[1], m[2]);
  }
  return map;
}

function read(rel) {
  const path = resolve(root, rel);
  return existsSync(path) ? parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8")) : new Map();
}

/** `shared` holds key values that already exist in the other .env file, by this file's variable name. */
function generate(name, value, infra, shared) {
  if (value.includes("change-me-key-") && shared.has(name)) return shared.get(name);
  if (value.startsWith("v1:change-me-key-")) return `v1:${randomBytes(32).toString("base64")}`;
  if (value.startsWith("change-me-key-")) return randomBytes(32).toString("base64");
  return value
    .replace(/change-me-(api|auth|migrate|notify|redis)(?![A-Za-z0-9_])/g, (match, role) => (role === "redis" ? infra.get("REDIS_PASSWORD") : infra.get(`KORBAT_${role.toUpperCase()}_DB_PASSWORD`)) ?? match)
    .replace(/change-me-[a-z]+/g, () => randomBytes(24).toString("hex"));
}

function complete(relExample, relTarget, infra, shared) {
  const example = readFileSync(resolve(root, relExample), "utf8");
  const targetPath = resolve(root, relTarget);

  if (!existsSync(targetPath)) {
    const lines = example.split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => {
      const m = LINE.exec(line);
      return m ? `${m[1]}=${generate(m[1], m[2], infra, shared)}` : line;
    });
    writeFileSync(targetPath, lines.join("\n"), "utf8");
    console.log(`${relTarget}: created with ${parse(example).size} keys`);
    return;
  }

  const current = readFileSync(targetPath, "utf8");
  const existing = parse(current);
  const added = [];
  let out = current.replace(/\s*$/, "\n");
  for (const [name, value] of parse(example)) {
    if (existing.has(name)) continue;
    out += `${name}=${generate(name, value, infra, shared)}\n`;
    added.push(name);
  }
  if (added.length === 0) {
    console.log(`${relTarget}: nothing to add`);
    return;
  }
  writeFileSync(targetPath, out, "utf8");
  console.log(`${relTarget}: completed, added ${added.join(", ")}`);
}

const LOCAL_HOSTS = ["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]"];
const existingOrigin = read("infra/.env").get("API_APP_ORIGIN");
if (existingOrigin !== undefined) {
  let host = "";
  try {
    host = new URL(existingOrigin).hostname;
  } catch {
    host = "";
  }
  if (!LOCAL_HOSTS.includes(host)) {
    console.error(`API_APP_ORIGIN in infra/.env is "${existingOrigin}", not a localhost origin. This script generates development values only; set production values by hand.`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

const hostApi = read("apps/api/.env");
complete("infra/.env.example", "infra/.env", new Map(), new Map([...hostApi].map(([name, value]) => [`API_${name}`, value])));

const infra = read("infra/.env");
const dockerApi = new Map([...infra].filter(([name]) => name.startsWith("API_")).map(([name, value]) => [name.slice("API_".length), value]));
complete("apps/api/.env.example", "apps/api/.env", infra, dockerApi);

/** A REDIS_URL written before Valkey required a password gains the one infra/.env holds. */
function addRedisPassword(relTarget, password) {
  if (!password) return;
  const path = resolve(root, relTarget);
  const current = readFileSync(path, "utf8");
  const line = current.split(/\r?\n/).find((l) => l.startsWith("REDIS_URL="));
  if (!line) return;
  const url = new URL(line.slice("REDIS_URL=".length));
  if (url.password) return;
  url.password = password;
  writeFileSync(path, current.replace(line, `REDIS_URL=${url.href}`), "utf8");
  console.log(`${relTarget}: REDIS_URL now carries the Valkey password`);
}
addRedisPassword("apps/api/.env", infra.get("REDIS_PASSWORD"));

complete("apps/app/.env.example", "apps/app/.env", new Map(), new Map());

// 3f: ntfy's configuration, a mounted file rather than variables (its password hashes hold $), from the example.
if (!existsSync(resolve(root, "infra/ntfy/server.yml"))) {
  copyFileSync(resolve(root, "infra/ntfy/server.yml.example"), resolve(root, "infra/ntfy/server.yml"));
  console.log("infra/ntfy/server.yml: created from its example (development users and tokens)");
}
complete("apps/worker/.env.example", "apps/worker/.env", new Map(), new Map());
// 3b: the importer run on the host (pnpm --filter @korbat/importer dev), on the folders apps/api/.env names for the API.
complete("apps/importer/.env.example", "apps/importer/.env", new Map(), new Map());

/** Rewrites apps/api/.env.test from apps/api/.env. Only where the data lives changes; every key stays the same. */
function deriveTestEnv() {
  const source = readFileSync(resolve(root, "apps/api/.env"), "utf8");
  const redisUrl = parse(source).get("REDIS_URL");
  const lines = source
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => {
      const m = LINE.exec(line);
      if (!m) return line;
      const [, name, value] = m;
      // 3f: the watcher's role too, whose URL the integration tests insert messages through.
      if (/^DATABASE_URL_(API|AUTH|MIGRATE|NOTIFY)$/.test(name)) {
        const url = new URL(value);
        if (!url.pathname.endsWith("_test")) url.pathname = `${url.pathname}_test`;
        return `${name}=${url.href}`;
      }
      if (name === "REDIS_URL") {
        const url = new URL(value);
        url.pathname = "/15";
        return `${name}=${url.href}`;
      }
      // 3d review: the recipients' count of the tests goes to the test Valkey's database 14, so the suite needs no counts
      // service and never touches the development one's.
      if (name === "COUNTS_URL") {
        const url = new URL(redisUrl ?? value);
        url.pathname = "/14";
        return `${name}=${url.href}`;
      }
      return line;
    });
  const header = "# Derived from apps/api/.env by scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs. Do not edit this file: rerun the script.";
  writeFileSync(resolve(root, "apps/api/.env.test"), [header, ...lines].join("\n"), "utf8");
  console.log("apps/api/.env.test: derived from apps/api/.env (test database, Redis databases 15 and 14)");
}

deriveTestEnv();
```
